Step 4 - Positional Tracking: Record the changing lunar position and phase at matching hours across four nights.

comparison_data.left_header: Req 6a: Lunar Topography And Landmark Sket
left_points: (6a) Lunar Topography And Landmark Sketching: Drawing the Moon requires identifying prominent features such as Mare Imbrium and crater Tycho. Observing near the terminator reveals sharp topographical relief across crater rims, central peaks, and ejecta blankets.

(6b) Multi Night Lunar Tracking Sketches: Daily observations at a consistent hour demonstrate the eastward orbital motion of the Moon. Recording horizon reference points illustrates daily phase transitions from crescent through gibbous forms.
right_points: (6c) Lunar Orbital Gravitational Mechanics: Earth gravitational force continuously accelerates the Moon inward while forward orbital velocity provides centripetal balance. This delicate equilibrium maintains a stable elliptical trajectory roughly two hundred thirty eight thousand miles away.

(6d) Lunar Phase And Eclipse Geometry: Relative spatial alignments of Sun, Earth, and Moon produce regular recurring lunar phases each month. Eclipses require the Moon to cross orbital node points directly aligned with the Sun and Earth.

rows.left: (6a) Lunar Seas and Crater Sketches: If you watch the Moon's position against the background stars, you will see that it also moves slowly eastward due to its orbit around the Earth (p. 43).
rows.right: (6c) Orbital Gravity and Inertia Balance: If you have trouble identifying craters, most public libraries have astronomy books with lunar maps (p. 43).

rows.left: (6b) Weekly Lunar Phase Observations: Draw the contours of visible features and label seas and prominent craters (p. 43).
rows.right: (6d) Solar and Lunar Eclipse Diagrams: Due to the rotation of the Earth, the Moon appears to travel westward since we see it rise in the east and set in the west (p. 43).

rows.left: Apparent Daily Westward Motion: Due to the rotation of the Earth, the Moon appears to travel westward since we see it rise in the east and set in the west (p. 43).

fields.Req 6a - Lunar Topography And Landmark S: Drawing the Moon requires identifying prominent features such as Mare Imbrium and crater Tycho. Observing near the terminator reveals sharp topographical relief across crater rims, central peaks, and ejecta blankets.
fields.Req 6b - Multi Night Lunar Tracking Sket: Daily observations at a consistent hour demonstrate the eastward orbital motion of the Moon. Recording horizon reference points illustrates daily phase transitions from crescent through gibbous forms.
fields.Req 6c - Lunar Orbital Gravitational Mec: Earth gravitational force continuously accelerates the Moon inward while forward orbital velocity provides centripetal balance. This delicate equilibrium maintains a stable elliptical trajectory roughly two hundred thirty eight thousand miles away.
fields.Req 6d - Lunar Phase And Eclipse Geometr: Relative spatial alignments of Sun, Earth, and Moon produce regular recurring lunar phases each month. Eclipses require the Moon to cross orbital node points directly aligned with the Sun and Earth.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: What two physical factors balance each other to keep the Moon in a stable orbit around Earth?
quiz_item.question: What two physical factors balance each other to keep the Moon in a stable orbit around Earth?
options: A. Solar wind pressure pushing outward and Earth's magnetic field pulling inward
B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
C. Atmospheric drag from the exosphere and tidal friction from Earth's oceans
D. Centrifugal spin from the Moon's core and radiation pressure from sunlight
choices: A. Solar wind pressure pushing outward and Earth's magnetic field pulling inward
B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
C. Atmospheric drag from the exosphere and tidal friction from Earth's oceans
D. Centrifugal spin from the Moon's core and radiation pressure from sunlight
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): The Moon stays in orbit because its forward orbital velocity (inertia) balances the inward gravitational attraction between Earth and the Moon (p. 43).

requirements.lead_text: With your counselor's approval and guidance, do ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: With your counselor's approval and guidance, do ONE of the following: (a) Visit a planetarium or astronomical observatory. Submit a written report, a scrapbook, OR a video presentation afterward to your counselor that includes the following information: activities occurring there, exhibits and displays you saw, telescopes and other instruments being used, and celestial objects you observed. (b) Plan and participate in an observation session that includes using binoculars or a telescope and includes at least 10 celestial objects beyond those observed in requirement 4. These might be lunar features, Messier objects, additional constellations or planets, or artificial satellites including the International Space Station. List the celestial objects you want to observe and find each in a star chart, guidebook or by using an app. Prepare a log or notebook. Discuss with your counselor what you hope to observe prior to your observation session. Review your log or notebook with your counselor afterward. (c) Plan and host a star party for your Scout troop or other group such as your class at school. Use binoculars or a telescope to show and explain celestial objects to the group. (d) Help an astronomy club in your community hold a star party that is open to the public. (e) Personally take a series of photographs or digital images of the movement of the Moon, a planet, an asteroid, meteor, or a comet. In your visual display, label each image and include the date and time it was taken. Show all positions on a star chart or map. Show your display at school or at a troop meeting. Explain the changes you observed. (f) With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, use online observing opportunities such as SkyNet to observe planets, comets, galaxies, and/or the sun. Describe your experience to your counselor.

options: A. It splits incoming light into a spectrum to identify chemical elements and measure motion toward or away from Earth
B. It amplifies sound waves traveling through space from stellar explosions
C. It shoots a laser beam at the star to measure the bounce-back time
D. It sweeps dust off the primary mirror during long photographic exposures

quiz_item.correct_answer: A. It splits incoming light into a spectrum to identify chemical elements and measure motion toward or away from Earth
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): By dispersing light into a spectrum, a spectrometer reveals unique elemental spectral lines and Doppler shifts that show composition and radial velocity (p. 64).

requirements.description: With your counselor's approval and guidance, do ONE of the following: (a) Visit a planetarium or astronomical observatory. Submit a written report, a scrapbook, OR a video presentation afterward to your counselor that includes the following information: activities occurring there, exhibits and displays you saw, telescopes and other instruments being used, and celestial objects you observed. (b) Plan and participate in an observation session that includes using binoculars or a telescope and includes at least 10 celestial objects beyond those observed in requirement 4. These might be lunar features, Messier objects, additional constellations or planets, or artificial satellites including the International Space Station. List the celestial objects you want to observe and find each in a star chart, guidebook or by using an app. Prepare a log or notebook. Discuss with your counselor what you hope to observe prior to your observation session. Review your log or notebook with your counselor afterward. (c) Plan and host a star party for your Scout troop or other group such as your class at school. Use binoculars or a telescope to show and explain celestial objects to the group. (d) Help an astronomy club in your community hold a star party that is open to the public. (e) Personally take a series of photographs or digital images of the movement of the Moon, a planet, an asteroid, meteor, or a comet. In your visual display, label each image and include the date and time it was taken. Show all positions on a star chart or map. Show your display at school or at a troop meeting. Explain the changes you observed. (f) With your parent or guardian's and counselor's approval, use online observing opportunities such as SkyNet to observe planets, comets, galaxies, and/or the sun. Describe your experience to your counselor.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: During a troop star party and daytime solar observation session for Astronomy Requirement 1, which safety and field practice is mandatory?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: During a troop star party and daytime solar observation session for Astronomy Requirement 1, which safety and field practice is mandatory?
options: A. View the Sun directly through binoculars while wearing polarized sunglasses, and use a bright white LED lantern at night to read star charts.

B. Never look at the Sun through any telescope, binoculars, or camera without a certified front-aperture solar filter or indirect pinhole projection, and use a dim red flashlight at night to preserve dark adaptation.
C. Thread a dark glass eyepiece filter onto the back of a large reflector telescope to view sunspots, and shine a green laser pointer into the eyes of observers to line up constellations.
D. Wipe morning dew off telescope objective lenses with a dry paper towel and warm frozen eyepieces over an open camp stove flame.
choices: A. View the Sun directly through binoculars while wearing polarized sunglasses, and use a bright white LED lantern at night to read star charts.

B. Never look at the Sun through any telescope, binoculars, or camera without a certified front-aperture solar filter or indirect pinhole projection, and use a dim red flashlight at night to preserve dark adaptation.
C. Thread a dark glass eyepiece filter onto the back of a large reflector telescope to view sunspots, and shine a green laser pointer into the eyes of observers to line up constellations.
D. Wipe morning dew off telescope objective lenses with a dry paper towel and warm frozen eyepieces over an open camp stove flame.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Never look at the Sun through any telescope, binoculars, or camera without a certified front-aperture solar filter or indirect pinhole projection, and use a dim red flashlight at night to preserve dark adaptation.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Looking at the Sun through unfiltered optics concentrates solar energy onto the retina and causes instant, permanent blindness; certified front-aperture solar filters or indirect projection are required, and red light preserves night vision.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do airborne dust, chemical pollution, and high humidity combined with city lights affect night sky observations?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do airborne dust, chemical pollution, and high humidity combined with city lights affect night sky observations?
options: A. They scatter artificial light across the sky and reduce transparency for faint objects
B. They act as a natural filter that sharpens the edges of bright planets
C. They only block radio waves and have no effect on visible starlight
D. They push turbulent air layers higher into the stratosphere to stop twinkling
choices: A. They scatter artificial light across the sky and reduce transparency for faint objects
B. They act as a natural filter that sharpens the edges of bright planets
C. They only block radio waves and have no effect on visible starlight
D. They push turbulent air layers higher into the stratosphere to stop twinkling
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. They scatter artificial light across the sky and reduce transparency for faint objects
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Airborne particles and moisture scatter artificial light from below to brighten sky glow while absorbing faint starlight from deep-sky objects (p. 24).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the main structural difference between a refracting telescope and a Newtonian reflecting telescope?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the main structural difference between a refracting telescope and a Newtonian reflecting telescope?
options: A. A refractor uses a curved primary mirror at the bottom of the tube, while a reflector uses only glass lenses
B. A refractor can only observe radio waves, while a reflector observes visible starlight
C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
D. A refractor requires an equatorial mount, while a reflector can only use an altazimuth mount
choices: A. A refractor uses a curved primary mirror at the bottom of the tube, while a reflector uses only glass lenses
B. A refractor can only observe radio waves, while a reflector observes visible starlight
C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
D. A refractor requires an equatorial mount, while a reflector can only use an altazimuth mount
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. A refractor gathers and focuses light with a front objective lens, while a reflector uses a curved primary mirror
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Refracting telescopes bend light through an objective lens at the front of the tube, whereas reflecting telescopes collect and focus light off a curved primary mirror at the rear (p. 56).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How should you orient a printed star chart when you are standing outside facing east to identify constellations?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How should you orient a printed star chart when you are standing outside facing east to identify constellations?
options: A. Hold the chart flat against the ground with north pointing toward your feet
B. Hold the chart overhead and rotate it until the east label is at the bottom
C. Always keep the north label at the bottom regardless of which direction you face
D. Flip the chart face-down and view it through a mirror
choices: A. Hold the chart flat against the ground with north pointing toward your feet
B. Hold the chart overhead and rotate it until the east label is at the bottom
C. Always keep the north label at the bottom regardless of which direction you face
D. Flip the chart face-down and view it through a mirror
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Hold the chart overhead and rotate it until the east label is at the bottom
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): To match a star chart to the real sky, hold it overhead and turn it so the compass direction you are facing is at the bottom of the chart (p. 9).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do Mercury and Venus exhibit crescent phases as seen from Earth while Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn do not?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do Mercury and Venus exhibit crescent phases as seen from Earth while Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn do not?
options: A. Mercury and Venus have thick cloud layers that block half of their sunlight
B. Outer planets spin too rapidly for telescopes to capture their crescent shadows
C. Earth's shadow falls directly across Mercury and Venus every month
D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
choices: A. Mercury and Venus have thick cloud layers that block half of their sunlight
B. Outer planets spin too rapidly for telescopes to capture their crescent shadows
C. Earth's shadow falls directly across Mercury and Venus every month
D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, allowing us to view their night sides as they pass between Earth and the Sun
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Because Mercury and Venus orbit closer to the Sun than Earth does, we view their sunlit hemispheres from changing angles, including a crescent when they pass nearly between Earth and the Sun (p. 35).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What two physical factors balance each other to keep the Moon in a stable orbit around Earth?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What two physical factors balance each other to keep the Moon in a stable orbit around Earth?
options: A. Solar wind pressure pushing outward and Earth's magnetic field pulling inward
B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
C. Atmospheric drag from the exosphere and tidal friction from Earth's oceans
D. Centrifugal spin from the Moon's core and radiation pressure from sunlight
choices: A. Solar wind pressure pushing outward and Earth's magnetic field pulling inward
B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
C. Atmospheric drag from the exosphere and tidal friction from Earth's oceans
D. Centrifugal spin from the Moon's core and radiation pressure from sunlight
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. The Moon's forward inertia of motion and the inward pull of gravity between Earth and the Moon
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): The Moon stays in orbit because its forward orbital velocity (inertia) balances the inward gravitational attraction between Earth and the Moon (p. 43).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What does a star's color (such as blue-white Rigel, yellow Capella, or red Betelgeuse) primarily reveal to astronomers?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What does a star's color (such as blue-white Rigel, yellow Capella, or red Betelgeuse) primarily reveal to astronomers?
options: A. Its exact distance in light-years from Earth
B. The number of rocky planets orbiting in its habitable zone
C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
D. Whether the star is located in the northern or southern celestial hemisphere
choices: A. Its exact distance in light-years from Earth
B. The number of rocky planets orbiting in its habitable zone
C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
D. Whether the star is located in the northern or southern celestial hemisphere
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Its surface temperature, with blue stars being the hottest and red stars being the coolest
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A star's color is a direct indicator of its surface temperature: blue stars are the hottest, yellow stars like the Sun are intermediate, and red stars are the coolest (p. 51).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does a spectrometer attached to an observatory telescope help astronomers study a distant star or galaxy?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does a spectrometer attached to an observatory telescope help astronomers study a distant star or galaxy?
options: A. It splits incoming light into a spectrum to identify chemical elements and measure motion toward or away from Earth
B. It amplifies sound waves traveling through space from stellar explosions
C. It shoots a laser beam at the star to measure the bounce-back time
D. It sweeps dust off the primary mirror during long photographic exposures
choices: A. It splits incoming light into a spectrum to identify chemical elements and measure motion toward or away from Earth
B. It amplifies sound waves traveling through space from stellar explosions
C. It shoots a laser beam at the star to measure the bounce-back time
D. It sweeps dust off the primary mirror during long photographic exposures
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. It splits incoming light into a spectrum to identify chemical elements and measure motion toward or away from Earth
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): By dispersing light into a spectrum, a spectrometer reveals unique elemental spectral lines and Doppler shifts that show composition and radial velocity (p. 64).

pamphlet_excerpts: Environmental Hazards: Extreme heat humidity and severe lightning storms present severe risks to outdoor athletes.
Tendon Protection: Acute sprains demand immediate rest ice compression and elevation to control internal swelling.
Fluid Balance: Dehydration degrades aerobic performance and increases the risk of dangerous heat exhaustion.
Blister Prevention: Clean synthetic socks reduce friction on damp skin to stop painful hot spots.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Hazard Assessment: Check the running track and turf field for holes glass and loose equipment.
Step 2 - Hydration Setup: Stage clean water coolers and individual squeeze bottles along the designated practice sideline.
Step 3 - First Aid Readiness: Position a fully stocked athletic medical kit adjacent to the team bench area.
Step 4 - Emergency Action: Rehearse exact communication duties for calling emergency services during sudden catastrophic athlete collapse.

pamphlet_excerpts: Physician Evaluation: Annual clinical examinations identify undetected cardiac murmurs and joint instability before vigorous training.
Immunization Records: Current tetanus boosters protect athletes from dangerous bacterial infections caused by open turf wounds.
Substance Dangers: Nicotine and alcohol degrade oxygen transport and slow muscle recovery after intense workouts.
Dietary Balance: Complex carbohydrates and lean proteins provide sustained glycogen storage for demanding sports activities.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Record Compilation: Gather past immunization cards and personal medical history documents before your clinical appointment.
Step 2 - Physician Screening: Complete a comprehensive physical exam covering resting pulse heart sounds and joint mobility.
Step 3 - Habit Inventory: Audit your daily sleep totals water consumption and dietary patterns using an honest journal.
Step 4 - Nutrition Planning: Structure balanced daily meals featuring whole grains fresh vegetables and high quality lean protein.

Progress Documentation: Tracking daily workout repetitions running times and perceived exertion highlights measurable physical improvements.
Footwear Selection: Activity specific athletic shoes support the foot arch and absorb damaging ground impact.

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Activity Selection: Choose one specific athletic discipline aligned with personal interests and local facility availability.
Step 2 - Baseline Testing: Record initial performance times jump distances or strength numbers under identical test conditions.
Step 3 - Training Execution: Execute progressive workouts three days each week while logging sets reps and times.
Step 4 - Progress Review: Analyze twelve weeks of training logs with your counselor to measure overall physical development.

pamphlet_excerpts: Official Rulebooks: Athletic governing bodies establish uniform standards ensuring competitive fairness and participant physical safety.
Dynamic Warmup: Light jogging and active mobility drills prepare muscles joints and nervous systems for exertion.
Amateur Principles: Amateur competitors participate purely for personal excellence and love of sport without financial compensation.
Respectful Conduct: Fair play demands treating opponents teammates and game officials with dignity and emotional control.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Rulebook Study: Review the official rule manuals governing your chosen sports with your merit badge counselor.
Step 2 - Warmup Execution: Perform ten minutes of dynamic movement drills including high knees butt kicks and skips.
Step 3 - Cooldown Routine: Conclude hard physical training with five minutes of walking followed by gentle static stretching.
Step 4 - Sportsmanship Discussion: Discuss real competitive scenarios where honoring ethical rules demonstrated true athletic character and maturity.

left_points: (4a) Athletic Rules and Regulations: Learning the official regulations of two athletic activities ensures fair competition and safe participation. Understanding rules allows players to compete effectively and avoid penalties.

(4b) Warmup and Cooldown Phases: Dynamic warmups elevate core body temperature and loosen joints, while cool downs restore resting heart rates. Both phases protect muscles from strains and facilitate metabolic recovery.
right_points: (4c) Amateur Versus Professional Athletics: Amateur athletes compete without direct financial compensation, pursuing sports for fitness, recreation, and character development. Professional athletes perform sports as their primary paid occupation.

(4d) Sportsmanship and Character Building: Good sportsmanship encompasses respect for officials, opponents, rules, and teammates regardless of victory or defeat. Demonstrating integrity on the field builds lasting personal character.

rows.right: (4c) Amateur Versus Professional Athletes: However, the rules changed in 1986 and professionals competed for the first time at the 1988 Olympic Games (p. 21).

rows.left: (4b) Warming Up and Cooling: When the modern Games began in 1896, only amateurs were allowed to compete (p. 21).
rows.right: (4d) Good Sportsmanship in Athletics: Regardless if they are considered amateur or professional, athletes should uphold high standards (p. 21).

requirements.lead_text: Complete the activities in FOUR of the following options and show improvement over a three-month period:
requirements.req_text: Complete the activities in FOUR of the following options and show improvement over a three-month period: (a) Option A, Sprinting. Do ALL of the following: (1) 100-meter dash (2) 200-meter dash (b) Option B, Long-Distance Running. Do ALL of the following: (1) 3k run (2) 5k run (c) Option C, Long Jump OR High Jump. Do ALL of the following: (1) Running long jump OR running high jump (best of three tries) (2) Standing long jump OR standing high jump (best of three tries) (d) Option D, Swimming. Do ALL of the following: (1) 100-meter swim (2) 200-meter swim (e) Option E, Pull-Ups AND Push-Ups. Do ALL of the following: (1) Pull-ups in two minutes (2) Push-ups in two minutes (f) Option F, Baseball Throw. Do ALL of the following: (1) Baseball throw for accuracy, 10 throws at a target (distance to be determined by age): ages 11 to 12, 20 feet; ages 13 to 15, 30 feet; ages 16 to 17, 40 feet (2) Baseball throw for distance, five throws (total distance) (g) Option G, Basketball Shooting. Do ALL of the following: (1) Basketball shot for accuracy, 10 free-throw shots (2) Basketball throw for skill and agility, the following shots: (a) Left-side layup (b) Right-side layup (c) Left side of hoop, along the key line (d) Right side of hoop, along the key line (e) Where key line and free-throw line meet, left side (f) Where key line and free-throw line meet, left side (g) Top of the key (h) Another spot along the three-point line (h) Option H, Football Kick OR Soccer Kick. Do ALL of the following: (1) Goals from the 10-yard line, eight kicks (2) Football kick or soccer kick for distance, five kicks (total distance) (i) Option I, Weight Training. Do ALL of the following: (1) Chest/bench press, two sets of 15 repetitions each (2) Leg curls, two sets of 15 repetitions each

left_points: (5a) Sprinting Speed and Mechanics: Sprinting demands maximum explosive speed, proper sprint mechanics, and fast acceleration out of the blocks. Tracking the 100-meter and 200-meter dash demonstrates improvements in stride turnover.

(5b) Long Distance Endurance Running: Distance running builds cardiovascular endurance, efficient breathing rhythms, and mental stamina over 3k and 5k courses. Proper pacing strategies prevent premature exhaustion during long races.

(5c) Jumping Power and Technique: Long jump and high jump require the conversion of horizontal velocity into explosive vertical lift. Practicing approach strides and takeoff mechanics yields greater height and distance.
right_points: (5e) Upper Body Calisthenics Testing: Pull-ups and push-ups measure relative upper body strength and core stabilization under standardized time limits. Consistent bodyweight calisthenics build muscular endurance in the back, chest, and arms.

(5f) Baseball Throwing Accuracy: Baseball throwing tests rotational power, shoulder coordination, and targeting accuracy at age-appropriate distances. Proper follow-through mechanics protect the throwing elbow while hitting target bullseyes.

(5g) Basketball Shooting and Agility: Basketball shooting drills evaluate fingertip touch, footwork, and balance during free throws and game-speed agility layups. Repetitive shooting routines reinforce motor memory and free-throw percentage.

Do ALL of the following: (1) Goals from the 10-yard line, eight kicks (2) Football kick or soccer kick for distance, five kicks (total distance) (i) Option I, Weight Training. intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-12-31). The Auctioneering Badge is a dynamic blend of public speaking and salesmanship that offers Scouts the opportunity to develop essential communication and persuasion skills. Scouts will learn about the history of auctioneering, develop presentation techniques, and build rapport with an audience. They’ll engage in mock auctions to practice creating demand and closing deals while also learning how to handle challenges and uphold ethical standards. This badge fosters confidence and critical thinking skills that are powerful tools for personal growth, leadership roles, and future success.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
quiz_item.question: During a live charity auction, a bidder raises their hand to place a $100 bid, and simultaneously a collaborator in the crowd places a fake 'shill' bid solely to artificially drive up the price without intending to buy. Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
options: A. Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
C. Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
D. Invent phantom bids from the podium after the reserve price has already been met.
choices: A. Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
C. Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
D. Invent phantom bids from the podium after the reserve price has already been met.
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Auctioneering ethics and state licensing laws require complete transparency in bid calling; undisclosed shill bidding is fraudulent and destroys buyer trust.

Step 4 - Settlement Walkthrough: Reconcile cashier receipts against the clerk book to confirm zero transaction discrepancies before release.

C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
D. Buyers must wait thirty days after the sale to learn what the final price will be
choices: A. The seller sets a price ceiling and buyers negotiate downward from that number
B. Government regulators assign a fixed value before any buyer can make an offer

quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit

quiz_item.question: What defines an absolute auction compared to a reserve auction?

B. Only licensed wholesale dealers are allowed to register for a bidder paddle
C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
D. Every bidder must submit a sealed envelope instead of bidding openly
choices: A. The seller may cancel the sale after the gavel falls if the price feels too low
B. Only licensed wholesale dealers are allowed to register for a bidder paddle
C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
D. Every bidder must submit a sealed envelope instead of bidding openly
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): An absolute auction has no minimum reserve price, meaning the property is sold to the highest bidder regardless of price, which attracts maximum buyer interest (p. 30).

pamphlet_excerpts: Chant Structure Basics: A chant alternates between the current bid accepted and the next bid requested.
Filler Word Purpose: Filler words smooth transitions between numbers while giving bidders brief moments to reflect.
Diaphragmatic Breath Control: Auctioneers breathe from the lower diaphragm to sustain vocal power through marathon sale sessions.
Number Articulation Drills: Daily recitation of counting sequences forward and backward trains vocal agility and speech clarity.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Breathing Exercises: Practice lower abdominal diaphragmatic breathing to support consistent vocal projection without straining vocal cords.
Step 2 - Number Articulation: Drill standard number progression sequences aloud to build crisp tongue and lip muscle memory.
Step 3 - Filler Integration: Introduce simple filler phrases between numbers to create a smooth, rhythmic bid calling cadence.
Step 4 - Public Demonstration: Perform your polished chant before your counselor and patrol during an official troop meeting.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: During a live charity auction, a bidder raises their hand to place a $100 bid, and simultaneously a collaborator in the crowd places a fake 'shill' bid solely to artificially drive up the price without intending to buy. Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: During a live charity auction, a bidder raises their hand to place a $100 bid, and simultaneously a collaborator in the crowd places a fake 'shill' bid solely to artificially drive up the price without intending to buy. Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
options: A. Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
C. Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
D. Invent phantom bids from the podium after the reserve price has already been met.
choices: A. Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
C. Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
D. Invent phantom bids from the podium after the reserve price has already been met.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Auctioneering ethics and state licensing laws require complete transparency in bid calling; undisclosed shill bidding is fraudulent and destroys buyer trust.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the primary responsibility of a ringperson (or bid spotter) during a live auction?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the primary responsibility of a ringperson (or bid spotter) during a live auction?
options: A. Recording the winning bidder number and final price in the official ledger
B. Spotting buyer bids in the crowd and relaying them clearly to the auctioneer
C. Processing credit card payments and issuing paid lot receipts to buyers
D. Signing the legal consignment contract with the property owner before the sale
choices: A. Recording the winning bidder number and final price in the official ledger
B. Spotting buyer bids in the crowd and relaying them clearly to the auctioneer
C. Processing credit card payments and issuing paid lot receipts to buyers
D. Signing the legal consignment contract with the property owner before the sale
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Spotting buyer bids in the crowd and relaying them clearly to the auctioneer
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Ring persons work the floor to spot bids in large crowds, communicate bid increments to buyers, and relay active bids directly to the auctioneer (p. 12).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does price discovery in an ascending-bid auction differ from a traditional fixed-price sale?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does price discovery in an ascending-bid auction differ from a traditional fixed-price sale?
options: A. The seller sets a price ceiling and buyers negotiate downward from that number
B. Government regulators assign a fixed value before any buyer can make an offer
C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
D. Buyers must wait thirty days after the sale to learn what the final price will be
choices: A. The seller sets a price ceiling and buyers negotiate downward from that number
B. Government regulators assign a fixed value before any buyer can make an offer
C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
D. Buyers must wait thirty days after the sale to learn what the final price will be
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Competitive bidding establishes true market value with no predetermined upper limit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Unlike fixed-price listings that cap what a seller can receive, competitive bidding in an auction allows buyers to push the price upward to true market value (p. 17).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens near the end of many online auctions that makes watching until the sale concludes essential?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens near the end of many online auctions that makes watching until the sale concludes essential?
options: A. All prior bids are erased and the auction restarts as a voice auction
B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
C. The website hides the current high bid so buyers must guess the price
D. Online auctions always close early as soon as three bids are placed
choices: A. All prior bids are erased and the auction restarts as a voice auction
B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
C. The website hides the current high bid so buyers must guess the price
D. Online auctions always close early as soon as three bids are placed
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Late bids often trigger soft-close time extensions to prevent last-second bid sniping
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Most online auction platforms use a staggered soft-close feature that extends the countdown clock by a few minutes whenever a last-second bid arrives (p. 25).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What defines an absolute auction compared to a reserve auction?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What defines an absolute auction compared to a reserve auction?
options: A. The seller may cancel the sale after the gavel falls if the price feels too low
B. Only licensed wholesale dealers are allowed to register for a bidder paddle
C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
D. Every bidder must submit a sealed envelope instead of bidding openly
choices: A. The seller may cancel the sale after the gavel falls if the price feels too low
B. Only licensed wholesale dealers are allowed to register for a bidder paddle
C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
D. Every bidder must submit a sealed envelope instead of bidding openly
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The item is guaranteed to sell to the highest bidder regardless of the final price
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): An absolute auction has no minimum reserve price, meaning the property is sold to the highest bidder regardless of price, which attracts maximum buyer interest (p. 30).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which two pieces of information must always be clearly understood in an auctioneer's chant?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which two pieces of information must always be clearly understood in an auctioneer's chant?
options: A. The original retail price of the item and the seller's home address
B. The total number of people in the room and the time remaining in the hour
C. The commission percentage and the state sales tax rate on each lot
D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
choices: A. The original retail price of the item and the seller's home address
B. The total number of people in the room and the time remaining in the hour
C. The commission percentage and the state sales tax rate on each lot
D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. The current bid the auctioneer has and the next bid amount being asked
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Every effective chant clearly communicates two numbers to the audience: the bid currently held ('have') and the next increment sought ('want') (p. 34).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why should every item in a unit auction be assigned a distinct lot number before the event starts?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why should every item in a unit auction be assigned a distinct lot number before the event starts?
options: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
B. Because state law requires a ten-digit barcode on Scout camping equipment
C. To prevent anyone from inspecting the items during the preview period
D. So the auctioneer never has to describe what the item is while on stage
choices: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
B. Because state law requires a ten-digit barcode on Scout camping equipment
C. To prevent anyone from inspecting the items during the preview period
D. So the auctioneer never has to describe what the item is while on stage
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. So the clerk can accurately track which item sold, for how much, and to which bidder number
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Numbering each lot before the sale allows the auctioneer, clerk, and cashier to track every transaction accurately from opening bid to final checkout (p. 41).

requirements.lead_text: Safety and Registration. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Safety and Registration. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter during automotive maintenance activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards. (b) Discuss with your counselor the safety equipment, tools, and clothing used while checking or repairing a motor vehicle. Use this equipment, tools, and/or clothing (when needed or called for) in meeting the requirements for this merit badge. (c) Explain the different ways motor vehicles are powered. (d) Explain the safety considerations when performing maintenance on a vehicle equipped with a high-voltage electrical system. (e) Review the maintenance chart in the vehicle owner's manual. Explain the requirements and time limits. (f) Explain the purpose, importance, and limitations of safety belts and passive restraints. (g) Find out the requirements for your state's emissions and safety inspections (as applicable), including how often a vehicle needs to be inspected. (h) Explain the importance of registering a vehicle and find out the annual registration fee for renewing your family car's registration.

pamphlet_excerpts: Hazard Prevention: Secure elevated vehicles on rated jack stands before placing any limb underneath.
Eye Protection: Wear ANSI Z87 approved safety glasses during all fluid checks and mechanical work.
Toxicity Control: Collect hazardous fluids in sealed containers to prevent skin contact and environmental runoff.
Electrical Safety: Disconnect the negative battery terminal before servicing any starting or charging circuit components.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Protective Equipment Setup: Put on ANSI rated safety glasses and chemical resistant nitrile gloves before starting.
Step 2 - Parking Brake Engagement: Shift into park, set the emergency brake, and place chocks behind opposite wheels.
Step 3 - High Voltage Clearance: Check for orange high voltage cables and turn off ignition keys completely.
Step 4 - Documentation Review: Open the vehicle owner manual to locate factory service schedules and registration records.

left_points: (1a) Automotive Shop Hazard Mitigation: Automotive maintenance introduces severe hazards including chemical exposure, mechanical pinch points, hot exhaust components, and heavy falling objects. Technicians anticipate risks by setting wheel chocks, confirming mechanical lockouts, and wearing appropriate protective gear.

(1b) Personal Protective Equipment Standards: Technicians must wear fitted cotton work clothes, steel-toed footwear, and impact-resistant safety glasses while working around rotating machinery. Rings, necklaces, and loose ties present severe entanglement risks around active drive belts and cooling fans.

(1c) Motor Vehicle Powertrain Architectures: Vehicles derive motive power from gasoline internal combustion, diesel compression ignition, hybrid gas-electric drivetrains, or pure battery electric motors. Each powertrain architecture requires distinct maintenance procedures and safety protocols.
right_points: (1e) Manufacturer Maintenance Schedule Interpretation: Owner manuals provide detailed mileage and calendar intervals for replacing vital fluids, friction materials, and air filters. Scouts must interpret both normal and severe operating schedules to preserve engine warranties.

(1f) Passenger Restraint System Dynamics: Three-point lap and shoulder belts secure occupants within the vehicle survival space, while supplemental restraint airbags cushion head impacts. Airbags can cause fatal concussive injuries if passengers fail to wear primary safety belts correctly.

(1g) State Emissions Inspection Mandates: State safety and emissions programs verify that running gear, braking systems, illumination devices, and catalytic emission controls satisfy environmental and public safety statutes. Testing cadence typically follows annual or biennial requirements depending on local municipal regulations.

rows.left: (1a) Automotive Maintenance Hazards: These devices stay in the steering wheel and dashboard until needed (p. 20).
rows.right: (1e) Owner's Manual Maintenance Schedule: These devices stay in the steering wheel and dashboard until needed (p. 20).

rows.left: (1b) Protective Gear and Safe Tools: They protect the driver and front-seat passenger (p. 20).
rows.right: (1f) Seat Belts and Passive Restraints: They protect the driver and front-seat passenger (p. 20).

rows.left: (1c) Vehicle Power train Types: Some cars also include side-impact airbags, which open if the car is hit from either side (p. 20).
rows.right: (1g) State Emissions and Safety Inspections: Some cars also include side-impact airbags, which open if the car is hit from either side (p. 20).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
quiz_item.question: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
options: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
choices: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Hydraulic jacks can fail or leak pressure without warning; a vehicle must always be supported on properly rated mechanical jack stands on level ground with wheels chocked before anyone works beneath it.

requirements.description: Safety and Registration. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter during automotive maintenance activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards. (b) Discuss with your counselor the safety equipment, tools, and clothing used while checking or repairing a motor vehicle. Use this equipment, tools, and/or clothing (when needed or called for) in meeting the requirements for this merit badge. (c) Explain the different ways motor vehicles are powered. (d) Explain the safety considerations when performing maintenance on a vehicle equipped with a high-voltage electrical system. (e) Review the maintenance chart in the vehicle owner's manual. Explain the requirements and time limits. (f) Explain the purpose, importance, and limitations of safety belts and passive restraints. (g) Find out the requirements for your state's emissions and safety inspections (as applicable), including how often a vehicle needs to be inspected. (h) Explain the importance of registering a vehicle and find out the annual registration fee for renewing your family car's registration.

requirements.lead_text: General Maintenance. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: General Maintenance. Do the following: (a) Demonstrate how to check the following: (1) Brake fluid (2) Engine oil (3) Coolant (4) Power steering fluid (5) Windshield washer fluid (6) Transmission fluid (7) Battery fluid (if possible) and condition of the battery terminals (b) Locate the fuse boxes; determine the type and size of fuses. Demonstrate the proper replacement of burned-out fuses. (c) Demonstrate how to check the condition and tension of belts and hoses. (d) Check the vehicle for proper operation of its lights, including the interior overhead lights, instrument lights, warning lights, and exterior bulbs. (e) Locate and check the air filter(s).

pamphlet_excerpts: Fluid Assessment: Examine fluid levels on level ground before starting or after adequate cooldown.
Circuit Protection: Match fuse amp ratings precisely to manufacturer board markings during circuit replacement.
Drive Belt Inspection: Twist serpentine belts outward to inspect ribs for cracking, fraying, or glaze.
Air Induction: Check pleated air filter elements against bright light to detect accumulated particulate.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Level Surface Preparation: Park the vehicle on level concrete, set the brake, and open the hood.
Step 2 - Primary Fluid Evaluation: Pull, wipe, and reinsert the engine oil dipstick to confirm proper oil level.
Step 3 - Circuit Fuse Extraction: Open the fuse distribution box and extract suspect fuses using an insulated puller.
Step 4 - Accessory Belt Check: Measure serpentine belt tension and examine the rubber under-ribs for dry rot cracks.
gear_checklist: ANSI Z87.1 safety glasses, digital multimeter (volt/ohm/ammeter), and insulated hand tools

left_points: (2a) Fluid Reservoir Inspection Protocols: Checking engine oil, transmission fluid, coolant, power steering, and brake fluid requires understanding individual reservoir dipsticks and sight glass indicators. Cold versus warm fluid expansion lines dictate exact fill targets across varied mechanical reservoirs.

(2b) Electrical Fuse Box Diagnostics: Fuse boxes protect vehicle wiring harnesses from electrical shorts and destructive current overloads. Burned-out fuses display broken fusible metal links and must be replaced using identical amperage ratings extracted with plastic fuse pullers.
right_points: (2c) Accessory Drive Belt Inspection: Technicians examine serpentine and V-belts for edge fraying, rubber cracking, longitudinal rib separation, and proper spring-loaded tensioner alignment. Radiator and heater hoses must be squeezed when cold to identify internal sponginess or heat-induced hardening.

(2d) Vehicle Lighting System Audit: A complete lighting audit encompasses headlights, daytime running lamps, turn signals, brake lamps, hazard flashers, and interior instrument clusters. Identifying burned-out bulbs ensures compliance with traffic statutes and alerts trailing motorists during deceleration.

rows.left: (2a) Essential Vehicle Fluid Checks: Modern serpentine belts do not show obvious wear; use amanufacturerapproved wear gauge to determine if replacement is needed (p. 16).
rows.right: (2c) Belt and Hose Inspection: To accurately check the tension of belts, you must use a belt tension gauge (p. 16).

rows.left: (2b) Fuse Box and Fuse Replacement: Belts and hoses that need to be replaced might feel brittle or mushy when you pinch them; they also might show cracks (p. 16).
rows.right: (2d) Interior and Exterior Light Checks: However, you can get a rough idea of tension by depressing the belt in the middle of its longest straight section (p. 16).

rows.left: Manual Belt Deflection Test: However, you can get a rough idea of tension by depressing the belt in the middle of its longest straight section (p. 16).
rows.right: (2e) Engine Air Filter Inspection: Modern serpentine belts do not show obvious wear; use amanufacturerapproved wear gauge to determine if replacement is needed (p. 16).

quiz_item.question: How should you determine if a modern serpentine belt needs to be replaced when it does not show obvious cracks?
options: A. Pour soapy water on the pulley while the engine is running
B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
C. Pry the belt off with a screwdriver to test its elasticity
D. Wait until the belt snaps or squeals loudly during highway driving

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs

pamphlet_excerpts: Placard Specifications: Inflate tires strictly according to vehicle door jamb placards rather than sidewall maxima.
Cold Pressure Measurement: Check inflation pressures using a calibrated gauge when tires are completely cold.
Alignment Geometry: Align caster, camber, and toe angles to prevent premature edge wear and pulling.
Wear Bar Limits: Replace tires immediately when tread depths wear flush with the wear indicators.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Specification Verification: Read the vehicle door jamb placard for front, rear, and spare cold pressures.
Step 2 - Pressure Gauge Reading: Remove the tire valve cap and press a calibrated gauge firmly against valve.
Step 3 - Chuck Air Adjustment: Add compressed air or bleed pressure until gauge matches door placard value exactly.
Step 4 - Tread Depth Evaluation: Inspect the lateral wear bars across tire grooves to confirm legal tread depth.

Drain Procedures: Drain spent coolant from the radiator petcock into dedicated sealed automotive waste containers.

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Cold System Confirmation: Ensure the engine has cooled completely before touching radiator or heater hoses.

pamphlet_excerpts: Air Fuel Stoichiometry: Computer systems maintain fourteen point seven to one air fuel ratios for complete combustion.
Intake Filtration: Pleated intake filters prevent particulate debris from damaging delicate mass airflow sensor wires.
Injector Metering: Electronic solenoids pulse high pressure fuel sprays into intake ports or combustion chambers.
Sensor Feedback: Heated oxygen sensors measure exhaust gas composition to adjust dynamic injector pulse widths.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Air Filter Housing Access: Unlatch the air cleaner housing clips and extract the pleated intake filter.
Step 2 - Sensor Wiring Inspection: Examine the electrical harness connector on the mass airflow sensor for corrosion.
Step 3 - Fuel Rail Observation: Locate the fuel rail, electronic injector harness clips, and intake manifold runners.
Step 4 - Fuel Filter Identification: Trace fuel supply lines from tank to locate external inline fuel filter canisters.

comparison_data.left_header: Req 7a: Air and Fuel Filtration Mechanics
left_points: (7a) Air and Fuel Filtration Mechanics: The induction system blends filtered atmospheric oxygen with pressurized fuel to achieve combustible mixtures inside cylinder heads. Air filters protect mass airflow sensors from debris, while fuel filters prevent rust and silt from clogging micron-sized injector pintles.
right_points: (7b) Electronic Fuel Injection Operation: Electronic fuel injection relies on an engine control module that processes throttle position, crankshaft angle, and oxygen sensor data to calculate injector pulse widths. Solenoid or piezoelectric injectors spray atomized fuel directly into intake runners or cylinder combustion bowls.

rows.left: (7a) Air and Fuel Filtration Systems: As mentioned earlier, automobile engines burn a mixture of fuel and air (p. 48).
rows.right: (7b) Computer-Controlled Fuel Injection: The air intake and fuel systems work together to create this mixture (p. 48).

rows.left: Coordinated Intake and Fueling: The air intake and fuel systems work together to create this mixture (p. 48).
rows.right: Step 2 - Burn Air-Fuel Cylinder Charge: The combustion process creates power by burning a mixture of air and gasoline (p. 48).

rows.left: Core Fuel System Principles: These systems may seem complex, but they rely on three basic principles, air-fuel mixture, pressure, and gasoline vaporization (p. 48).
rows.right: Step 3 - Adjust Mixture For Conditions: The AIR GAS RICH amounts of each, however, change all the time 8 TO 1 because of differences in temperature, vehicles peed, and terrain (p. 48).

comparison_data.left_header: Req 8a: Starting and Charging System Compo
left_points: (8a) Starting and Charging System Components: Vehicle electrical architectures integrate a storage battery, starter motor, and belt-driven alternator to manage electrical demands. Lighting and auxiliary systems draw regulated direct current power through fused circuits protected by electronic relays.

(8b) Engine Cylinder Firing Orders: Engine firing orders establish the precise sequence in which individual spark plugs ignite compressed air-fuel charges across cylinders. Distributing power strokes evenly balances rotational forces along the crankshaft, preventing excessive mechanical vibration.

(8c) Spark Plug Gap Calibration: The spark plug gap provides the physical separation across which ignition coils discharge thousands of volts to ignite the air-fuel mixture. Setting the gap to exact manufacturer tolerances ensures reliable flame kernel propagation and prevents engine misfires.
right_points: (8d) Safe Battery Jumper Connections: Jumping a dead vehicle battery requires strict attachment sequences to avoid sparking near explosive hydrogen gas pockets. Clamping positive cables first and ending with an unpainted engine block ground prevents hazardous battery explosions.

(8e) Electric Vehicle Range Factors: Electrified vehicle range depends on battery pack temperature, aggressive acceleration habits, aerodynamic drag, and auxiliary cabin heating loads. Recharging involves connecting dedicated Level 1, Level 2, or direct current fast-charging connectors through standardized charge ports.

(8f) Electrical Subsystem Dependencies: A stable electrical system powers electronic control modules, electric power steering racks, antilock braking solenoids, and safety sensors. Voltage drops trigger sensor calibration faults and induce transmission limp-mode lockouts.

pamphlet_excerpts: Drivetrain Architecture: Torque flows from engine flywheel through transmission, driveshafts, and differentials to driving wheels.
Transmission Diversity: Manual gearboxes use mechanical friction clutches while automatics employ hydraulic torque converters.
Hydraulic Fluid: Automatic transmission fluids lubricate planetary gearsets, cool clutches, and transmit hydraulic pressure.
Gearbox Lubrication: Heavy hypoid gear oils protect differential ring and pinion teeth from extreme shear.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Undercarriage Inspection: Safely elevate the vehicle to trace the transmission, driveshaft, and rear axle.
Step 2 - Differential Identification: Locate the differential housing and identify the fluid level inspection fill plug.
Step 3 - Transmission Fluid Check: Check automatic transmission dipstick with warm running engine parked on level concrete.
Step 4 - Transfer Case Audit: Identify the transfer case assembly on four-wheel drive configurations behind transmission.

left_points: (9a) Drivetrain Component Architecture: The drivetrain consists of the transmission, driveshafts, universal or constant-velocity joints, differential gears, and drive axles. These components multiply engine torque and transmit rotational power smoothly across flexible suspension geometries.

(9b) Transmission Mechanism Comparison: Manual transmissions require driver-actuated mechanical friction clutches to disengage gears during gear changes. Automatic transmissions utilize torque converters and electronically controlled planetary gearsets to execute smooth gear ratio shifts automatically.
right_points: (9c) Automatic Transmission Fluid Specifications: Automatic transmission fluids feature unique friction modifier formulations, detergent packages, and viscosity characteristics engineered for specific manufacturer transmissions. Utilizing unapproved fluid specifications causes internal wet clutch slippage and overheating.

(9d) Gearbox and Differential Lubricants: Manual transmissions, transfer cases, and differentials require high-viscosity gear lubricants engineered for extreme pressures and hypoid bevel gear shear forces. Hypoid gear lubricants protect differential ring and pinion teeth under heavy towing loads.

pamphlet_excerpts: Hydraulic Principles: Incompressible brake fluid transmits master cylinder hydraulic pressure instantaneously to caliper pistons.
Antilock Operation: Antilock brake modulators rapidly pulse hydraulic pressure to prevent wheel lockup during stops.
Friction Design: Disc brakes clamp spinning flat rotors while drum brakes expand shoes outward inside drums.
Lining Inspection: Measure brake friction pad thickness against factory minimum discard limits using thickness gauges.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Master Cylinder Check: Inspect the translucent brake master cylinder reservoir to verify fluid level and clarity.
Step 2 - Wheel Assembly Removal: Loosen lug nuts, elevate vehicle onto jack stands, and remove the wheel assembly.
Step 3 - Caliper Pad Inspection: Look through the caliper inspection port to measure the remaining friction lining thickness.
Step 4 - Rotor Surface Evaluation: Examine the brake rotor face for deep grooves, heat scoring, and rust lips.

requirements.lead_text: Do TWO of the following:
requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Determine the value of three different vehicles you are interested in purchasing. One must be new and one must be used; the third vehicle can be new or used. For each vehicle, find out the requirements and cost of automobile insurance to include basic liability and options for collision, comprehensive, towing, and rental car. Using the three vehicles you chose and with your counselor's assistance, complete the operation/maintenance chart provided in the Automotive Maintenance merit badge pamphlet. Use this information to determine the operating cost per mile for each vehicle, and discuss what you learn with your counselor. (b) Choose a car cleaner and wax product for a vehicle you want to clean. Explain clear-coat paint and the precautions necessary for care. Clean the vehicle, both inside and out, and wax the exterior. Use a vinyl and rubber protectant (on vinyl tops, rubber door seals, sidewalls, etc.) and explain the importance of this protectant. (c) Locate the manufacturer's jack. Use the jack to demonstrate how to engage the jack correctly on the vehicle, then change a tire correctly. (d) Perform an oil filter and oil change on a vehicle. Explain how to properly dispose of the used oil and filter.

Paint Preservation: Wash clear-coat finishes with balanced automotive soaps to avoid stripping protective wax layers.
Lifting Protocols: Position emergency jacks strictly beneath reinforced factory pinch welds to prevent structural collapse.
Oil Service: Replace drain plug crush washers and lubricate new oil filter rubber gaskets before installation.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Vehicle Jack Positioning: Locate the reinforced jacking notch along the vehicle rocker panel pinch weld seam.
Step 2 - Controlled Jack Elevation: Turn the jack screw clockwise until the flat tire clears the ground completely.
Step 3 - Oil Drain Plug Extraction: Place an oil drain pan beneath the crankcase and loosen the drain plug.
Step 4 - Gasket Lubrication Install: Smear fresh motor oil on the new filter gasket and spin it hand-tight.

B. They only wash and wax the exterior of vehicles at dealerships
C. They must diagnose complex electronics like engine control units and onboard diagnostics in addition to mechanical parts
D. They work exclusively from home offices using remote software updates
choices: A. They no longer use any wrenches, sockets, or hydraulic lifts in the shop
B. They only wash and wax the exterior of vehicles at dealerships
C. They must diagnose complex electronics like engine control units and onboard diagnostics in addition to mechanical parts
D. They work exclusively from home offices using remote software updates
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. They must diagnose complex electronics like engine control units and onboard diagnostics in addition to mechanical parts
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Working on today's sophisticated vehicles requires mastering electronic systems like the engine control unit and onboard diagnostics, not just hand tools (p. 94).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
options: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
choices: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Hydraulic jacks can fail or leak pressure without warning; a vehicle must always be supported on properly rated mechanical jack stands on level ground with wheels chocked before anyone works beneath it.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How should you determine if a modern serpentine belt needs to be replaced when it does not show obvious cracks?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How should you determine if a modern serpentine belt needs to be replaced when it does not show obvious cracks?
options: A. Pour soapy water on the pulley while the engine is running
B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
C. Pry the belt off with a screwdriver to test its elasticity
D. Wait until the belt snaps or squeals loudly during highway driving
choices: A. Pour soapy water on the pulley while the engine is running
B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
C. Pry the belt off with a screwdriver to test its elasticity
D. Wait until the belt snaps or squeals loudly during highway driving
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Use a manufacturer-approved wear gauge to inspect the belt ribs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Because modern serpentine belts rarely show obvious cracking, technicians use a manufacturer-approved belt wear gauge to check whether the ribs are worn down (p. 16).

options: A. The windshield washer fluid reservoir is completely empty
B. The vehicle is overdue for an exterior wash and wax treatment
C. One of the engine's emissions control systems may have a problem
D. The high-beam headlights are currently switched on
choices: A. The windshield washer fluid reservoir is completely empty
B. The vehicle is overdue for an exterior wash and wax treatment
C. One of the engine's emissions control systems may have a problem
D. The high-beam headlights are currently switched on
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. One of the engine's emissions control systems may have a problem
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The malfunction indicator lamp, commonly called the check engine light, illuminates when the onboard computer detects a problem in an engine or emissions control system (p. 85).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: If the pressure molded on the tire sidewall differs from the recommended pressure on the vehicle's door jamb placard, which pressure should you use?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: If the pressure molded on the tire sidewall differs from the recommended pressure on the vehicle's door jamb placard, which pressure should you use?
options: A. Always inflate the tire to the maximum pressure stamped on the tire sidewall
B. Average the two numbers together and add 5 psi for highway driving
C. Let air out until the tire sidewall bulges slightly on level pavement
D. Use the recommended inflation pressure noted on the vehicle
choices: A. Always inflate the tire to the maximum pressure stamped on the tire sidewall
B. Average the two numbers together and add 5 psi for highway driving
C. Let air out until the tire sidewall bulges slightly on level pavement
D. Use the recommended inflation pressure noted on the vehicle
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Use the recommended inflation pressure noted on the vehicle
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): The tire sidewall shows the maximum pressure the tire can hold, so you should always use the vehicle manufacturer's recommended pressure listed on the car (p. 39).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does a battery electric vehicle (EV) generate motion compared to a traditional gasoline car?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does a battery electric vehicle (EV) generate motion compared to a traditional gasoline car?
options: A. It uses an electric motor powered by electricity stored in a large battery pack
B. It burns liquid hydrogen inside a four-stroke piston cylinder block
C. It uses a diesel generator in the trunk that runs continuously at idle
D. It relies on compressed air tanks that refill at gas stations
choices: A. It uses an electric motor powered by electricity stored in a large battery pack
B. It burns liquid hydrogen inside a four-stroke piston cylinder block
C. It uses a diesel generator in the trunk that runs continuously at idle
D. It relies on compressed air tanks that refill at gas stations
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. It uses an electric motor powered by electricity stored in a large battery pack
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Instead of burning gasoline in an internal combustion engine, an EV uses an electric motor powered by a large rechargeable battery pack (p. 30).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What temperature protection does an equal 50/50 mixture of water and ethylene-glycol antifreeze provide during winter?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What temperature protection does an equal 50/50 mixture of water and ethylene-glycol antifreeze provide during winter?
options: A. It protects the engine only down to 32 degrees Fahrenheit
B. It protects the engine down to about 35 degrees below zero Fahrenheit
C. It prevents freezing only if the engine stays idling overnight
D. It freezes at 10 degrees Fahrenheit unless extra water is added
choices: A. It protects the engine only down to 32 degrees Fahrenheit
B. It protects the engine down to about 35 degrees below zero Fahrenheit
C. It prevents freezing only if the engine stays idling overnight
D. It freezes at 10 degrees Fahrenheit unless extra water is added
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It protects the engine down to about 35 degrees below zero Fahrenheit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Manufacturers generally recommend a 50/50 mixture of water and ethylene-glycol antifreeze, which protects the cooling system down to about -35 degrees Fahrenheit (p. 60).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What air-to-gasoline ratio allows an engine to achieve the most complete combustion and the lowest exhaust emissions?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What air-to-gasoline ratio allows an engine to achieve the most complete combustion and the lowest exhaust emissions?
options: A. 1 part air to 1 part gasoline
B. 5 parts air to 2 parts gasoline
C. 14.7 parts air to 1 part gasoline
D. 50 parts air to 1 part gasoline
choices: A. 1 part air to 1 part gasoline
B. 5 parts air to 2 parts gasoline
C. 14.7 parts air to 1 part gasoline
D. 50 parts air to 1 part gasoline
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. 14.7 parts air to 1 part gasoline
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A gasoline engine achieves the most complete combustion and lowest emissions when mixing 14.7 parts of air with 1 part of gasoline (p. 48).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What component in the charging system prevents the alternator from overcharging the vehicle's battery?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What component in the charging system prevents the alternator from overcharging the vehicle's battery?
options: A. The starter solenoid switch
B. The door jamb plunger switch
C. The spark plug electrode gap
D. The voltage regulator
choices: A. The starter solenoid switch
B. The door jamb plunger switch
C. The spark plug electrode gap
D. The voltage regulator
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. The voltage regulator
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A voltage regulator monitors system voltage and controls the amount of recharging current sent from the alternator to the battery (p. 69).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do the gears inside a car transmission differ from the chain rings and sprockets on a bicycle?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do the gears inside a car transmission differ from the chain rings and sprockets on a bicycle?
options: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
B. Any input gear can slide sideways to connect with any output gear at random
C. A rubber belt jumps from sprocket to sprocket each time the driver shifts
D. Car transmissions have only one fixed gear ratio for both hills and highways
choices: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
B. Any input gear can slide sideways to connect with any output gear at random
C. A rubber belt jumps from sprocket to sprocket each time the driver shifts
D. Car transmissions have only one fixed gear ratio for both hills and highways
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. The gears on the input and output shafts are always connected in dedicated pairs
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Unlike a bicycle where any chain ring can pair with any rear sprocket, the gears on a car transmission's input and output shafts are always connected in matched pairs (p. 33).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Model Axis Demonstration: Position the miniature aircraft along the pitch, roll, and yaw geometric axes.

Step 4 - Gyroscopic Instrument Review: Observe the attitude indicator gimbal mechanism responding to simulated bank angle changes.
