requirements.description: Cyber Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Attacks. Do the following and discuss each with your counselor: (a) Define the terms vulnerability, threat, and exploit, and give an example of each that might apply to a website or software product you use. (b) Pick one type of malware (such as virus, worm, Trojan, backdoor, spyware, or ransomware) and find out how it works. Explain what it does and the harm it can cause. (c) Identify two risks of using public Wi-Fi and describe how to reduce or avoid those risks. (d) Describe what spoofing and phishing are, and how to recognize a message or website that might be trying to trick you. Explain what steps you should take to protect yourself and others if you come across one. (e) Current Events. Do ONE of the following: (1) Read an article or a news report about a recent cybersecurity incident, such as a data breach or malware infection. Explain how the incident happened (to the best of your ability based on the information available) and what the consequences are or might be to the victim. (2) With your parent or guardian's permission, watch a movie or read a book in which cybersecurity plays a significant role. Discuss how cybersecurity topics were depicted and how realistic you think it was. (f) Create a list of what is part of your cyber attack surface including all the ways someone could try to access your personal information or devices, such as online accounts, apps, or home networks.

requirements.pamphlet_summary: Security risk involves recognizing how active threats exploit system flaws to breach defenses. Identifying malware behaviors, wireless risks, and deceptive engineering safeguards personal systems.
socratic_questions: How can an attacker impersonate a legitimate school portal on an open wireless network?
What psychological triggers in a phishing email tempt users to click suspicious links?
Why does reducing the number of installed phone applications shrink your attack surface?

requirements.lead_text: Cyber Defenses. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Cyber Defenses. Do the following: (a) Describe three technologies that are used to defend a computer or network, such as access controls, antivirus software, firewall, intrusion detection/prevention systems, and Virtual Private Network. (b) Installing updates. Do the following: (1) Explain to your counselor the importance of installing the latest updates on your computer, why they are needed, and what kinds of problems they can prevent. (2) Demonstrate to your counselor how to check for, download, and install the latest updates for your computer or mobile device, or another computer you have permission to use. (If you are unable to do this on your computer, you may use an online guide with screenshots to demonstrate this.) Show your counselor how to verify that your computer or mobile device is up-to-date. (c) System security. With your parent or guardian's permission, do THREE of the following using a computer or mobile device, and discuss with your counselor: (1) Describe what makes a good password and why. Set or change an account password to one that is "strong." (2) Describe multi-factor authentication (MFA) and how it can be used to improve security. Demonstrate how to use an authenticator app or other MFA function. (3) Install and set up a password manager. Demonstrate how it works to your counselor. (4) Run a virus scan. Show the results to your counselor. (5) Using a command line or other built-in tool, see what programs or processes are running on your computer. Discuss with your counselor what you see and what surprises you. (6) Use a command line interface to view your computer's open network connections. Discuss the results with your counselor. (7) Demonstrate how to back up your data from a mobile device to a local computer or the cloud. (8) Research best practices for protecting a home computer or network, and make a checklist of FIVE things you and your family can do to stay secure. (9) Identify one or more other vulnerabilities on your home computer or network or another computer or network you have permission to use and discuss with your counselor. With permission from the system owner, take the necessary actions to fix it.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: System security. With your parent or guardian's permission, do THREE of the following using a computer or mobile device, and discuss with your counselor: (1) Describe what makes a good password and why. Set or change an account password to one that is "strong." (2) Describe multi-factor authentication (MFA) and how it can be used to improve security. Demonstrate how to use an authenticator app or other MFA function. (3) Install and set up a password manager. Demonstrate how it works to your counselor. (4) Run a virus scan. Show the results to your counselor. (5) Using a command line or other built-in tool, see what programs or processes are running on your computer. Discuss with your counselor what you see and what surprises you. (6) Use a command line interface to view your computer's open network connections. Discuss the results with your counselor. (7) Demonstrate how to back up your data from a mobile device to a local computer or the cloud. (8) Research best practices for protecting a home computer or network, and make a checklist of FIVE things you and your family can do to stay secure. (9) Identify one or more other vulnerabilities on your home computer or network or another computer or network you have permission to use and discuss with your counselor. With permission from the system owner, take the necessary actions to fix.

pamphlet_excerpts: Firewall Packet Filtering: Network firewalls inspect incoming transmission packets to block unauthorized external access attempts.
Automated Software Updates: Applying vendor security updates closes known system vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them.
Strong Passphrase Construction: Combining multiple unrelated dictionary words creates high-entropy credentials resistant to cracking.
Multi-Factor Authentication Value: Secondary verification codes prevent account takeovers even when primary passwords become compromised.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Defense Review: Research operational mechanisms of firewalls, intrusion detection engines, and virtual private networks.
Step 2 - Update Verification: Check operating system patch levels and enable automatic security update delivery mechanisms.
Step 3 - Password Evaluation: Construct high-entropy passphrases exceeding sixteen characters with diverse symbols and numbers.
Step 4 - Multi-Factor Setup: Configure time-based one-time password authenticators on essential personal email or gaming accounts.

B. They patch known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and apps that attackers actively exploit
C. They automatically delete all your personal documents to free up hard drive space every month
D. They replace the need for strong passwords and multi-factor authentication on web accounts

requirements.lead_text: Cryptography. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Cryptography. Do the following: (a) Research and explain to your counselor three situations where encryption is used in cybersecurity. For each situation, describe what kind of encryption is used and why it is important. (b) Show how you can know if your connection to a website is encrypted. (c) Do ONE of the following: (1) Create your own encryption code, such as a substitution cipher or code book, and demonstrate using it to encrypt and decrypt a message. Describe the strengths and weaknesses of your code. (2) Download and set up an app (from an official app store) that uses end-to-end encryption. Explain to your counselor what this means, how it works, and why it is more secure than other forms of communication (e. g. SMS). (3) Use a hashing tool (for example, using SHA or MD5) to create a checksum for a file, document, or piece of text. Have a fellow Scout or your counselor make a change to it, then recreate the checksum and compare the new checksum to the original as a demonstration of file integrity checking. (4) Create your own PGP (pretty good privacy) email key. Share your public key with others (and your counselor). Also, get their public keys and add them to your computer's key ring. Send a message that has been digitally encrypted.

sub_requirements.text: Do ONE of the following: (1) Create your own encryption code, such as a substitution cipher or code book, and demonstrate using it to encrypt and decrypt a message. Describe the strengths and weaknesses of your code. (2) Download and set up an app (from an official app store) that uses end-to-end encryption. Explain to your counselor what this means, how it works, and why it is more secure than other forms of communication (e. g. SMS). (3) Use a hashing tool (for example, using SHA or MD5) to create a checksum for a file, document, or piece of text. Have a fellow Scout or your counselor make a change to it, then recreate the checksum and compare the new checksum to the original as a demonstration of file integrity checking. (4) Create your own PGP (pretty good privacy) email key. Share your public key with others (and your counselor). Also, get their public keys and add them to your computer's key ring. Send a message that has been digitally encrypted.

pamphlet_excerpts: Asymmetric Key Handshake: Public key infrastructure exchanges encryption keys safely across insecure public transmission routes.
Browser Certificate Validation: Web browsers verify domain ownership by checking digital certificates issued by authorities.
Substitution Cipher Mechanics: Classical Caesar ciphers shift plaintext letters by fixed alphabetical index offsets predictably.
Frequency Analysis Flaws: Common language letter frequencies reveal monoalphabetic substitution ciphers to experienced cryptanalysts.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Algorithm Exploration: Research symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic algorithms used to secure stored database records.
Step 2 - Certificate Inspection: Inspect web browser lock icons to verify public key certificate validity dates.
Step 3 - Cipher Construction: Build a substitution cipher wheel to encode and decode short plaintext messages.
Step 4 - Cryptanalysis Demonstration: Analyze letter frequencies in ciphertext to identify common English language character patterns.

pamphlet_excerpts: Smart Appliance Risks: Internet connected household devices often run outdated firmware with hardcoded default passwords.
Network Segmentation Defenses: Isolating smart appliances on separate virtual local networks protects family computing devices.
Remote Sensor Utilities: Connected thermostats adjust indoor climate automatically based on real-time household occupancy sensors.
Firmware Patching Protocols: Installing vendor security firmware remediates discovered vulnerabilities in embedded device microcontrollers.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Device Inventory: Identify four connected consumer electronic devices present in modern smart home households.
Step 2 - Benefit Analysis: Document operational conveniences provided by remote wireless connectivity on chosen smart appliances.
Step 3 - Risk Assessment: Analyze vulnerabilities arising from unpatched embedded firmware and hardcoded manufacturer passwords.
Step 4 - Defense Planning: Outline mitigation steps including guest network isolation and administrative password changes.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Cybersecurity Requirement 1, how do the three pillars of the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability) protect an organization's information systems?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Cybersecurity Requirement 1, how do the three pillars of the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability) protect an organization's information systems?
options: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
B. Confidentiality means keeping software bugs secret from programmers, Integrity means never updating operating systems, and Availability means posting all employee passwords on a public webpage.
C. The CIA Triad requires sharing a single administrator password across all staff members so nobody is ever locked out of the network.
D. Confidentiality deletes all files after twenty-four hours, Integrity blocks antivirus scanners, and Availability disables multi-factor authentication.
choices: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
B. Confidentiality means keeping software bugs secret from programmers, Integrity means never updating operating systems, and Availability means posting all employee passwords on a public webpage.
C. The CIA Triad requires sharing a single administrator password across all staff members so nobody is ever locked out of the network.
D. Confidentiality deletes all files after twenty-four hours, Integrity blocks antivirus scanners, and Availability disables multi-factor authentication.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data (via encryption and access controls), Integrity ensures data is not secretly altered or tampered with (via cryptographic hashes), and Availability ensures authorized users can reliably access systems when needed (via backups and DDoS mitigation).
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The CIA Triad is the core model of information security: Confidentiality protects privacy, Integrity guards accuracy and trustworthiness against tampering, and Availability keeps systems operational for legitimate users.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: If you accidentally discover an unprotected folder containing student grades on a school network, what is the ethical action that aligns with the Scout Law?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: If you accidentally discover an unprotected folder containing student grades on a school network, what is the ethical action that aligns with the Scout Law?
options: A. Publicly posting the vulnerability on social media so users are warned immediately
B. Downloading a few sample records to prove to your friends that the database is insecure
C. Immediately stopping access and privately reporting the flaw to the teacher or system administrator
D. Fixing the school database yourself by logging into the administrator account without asking
choices: A. Publicly posting the vulnerability on social media so users are warned immediately
B. Downloading a few sample records to prove to your friends that the database is insecure
C. Immediately stopping access and privately reporting the flaw to the teacher or system administrator
D. Fixing the school database yourself by logging into the administrator account without asking
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Immediately stopping access and privately reporting the flaw to the teacher or system administrator
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A Scout is trustworthy and obedient in cyberspace by respecting intellectual property, never accessing unauthorized accounts, and reporting security flaws responsibly to system owners (p. 8).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: If an attacker secretly alters the account balances in a bank database without stealing the data or taking the server offline, which principle of the C.I.A. Triad was primarily violated?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: If an attacker secretly alters the account balances in a bank database without stealing the data or taking the server offline, which principle of the C.I.A. Triad was primarily violated?
options: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
B. Confidentiality, because the website was temporarily unreachable during the afternoon
C. Availability, because an unauthorized person read private messages without changing them
D. Non-repudiation, because the server hardware ran out of backup battery power
choices: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
B. Confidentiality, because the website was temporarily unreachable during the afternoon
C. Availability, because an unauthorized person read private messages without changing them
D. Non-repudiation, because the server hardware ran out of backup battery power
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Integrity, because unauthorized modification compromised the accuracy and trustworthiness of the data
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Integrity ensures that data remains accurate, complete, and unaltered by unauthorized users while stored or in transit (p. 6).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is a primary risk of connecting to an open public Wi-Fi hotspot at a coffee shop, and how can you reduce that risk?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is a primary risk of connecting to an open public Wi-Fi hotspot at a coffee shop, and how can you reduce that risk?
options: A. Public Wi-Fi signals drain laptop batteries faster and corrupt local hard drive sectors
B. Public routers automatically install ransomware onto every device that connects without a password
C. Turning off your device firewall on public Wi-Fi is required so encrypted websites load properly
D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
choices: A. Public Wi-Fi signals drain laptop batteries faster and corrupt local hard drive sectors
B. Public routers automatically install ransomware onto every device that connects without a password
C. Turning off your device firewall on public Wi-Fi is required so encrypted websites load properly
D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Attackers can eavesdrop on unencrypted traffic or spoof the hotspot name, which you can mitigate by using a VPN and avoiding sensitive logins
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Public Wi-Fi networks allow attackers on the same network to intercept unencrypted traffic or set up evil-twin rogue hotspots; using a VPN and HTTPS websites protects your data in transit (p. 7).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is enabling automatic operating system and application updates one of the most effective cyber defenses?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is enabling automatic operating system and application updates one of the most effective cyber defenses?
options: A. They only add new cosmetic icons and slow down older computers without improving security
B. They patch known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and apps that attackers actively exploit
C. They automatically delete all your personal documents to free up hard drive space every month
D. They replace the need for strong passwords and multi-factor authentication on web accounts
choices: A. They only add new cosmetic icons and slow down older computers without improving security
B. They patch known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and apps that attackers actively exploit
C. They automatically delete all your personal documents to free up hard drive space every month
D. They replace the need for strong passwords and multi-factor authentication on web accounts
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. They patch known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and apps that attackers actively exploit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Software updates and security patches fix newly discovered vulnerabilities in operating systems and applications before attackers can exploit them (p. 8).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How can you verify that your connection to a website is encrypted before entering login credentials or payment details?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How can you verify that your connection to a website is encrypted before entering login credentials or payment details?
options: A. The website page background uses dark mode and displays a copyright notice at the bottom
B. The website URL ends with .org or .com instead of an IP address
C. The browser address bar uses https:// and displays a valid TLS security certificate for that domain
D. The website loads in less than two seconds without showing any pop-up advertisements
choices: A. The website page background uses dark mode and displays a copyright notice at the bottom
B. The website URL ends with .org or .com instead of an IP address
C. The browser address bar uses https:// and displays a valid TLS security certificate for that domain
D. The website loads in less than two seconds without showing any pop-up advertisements
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. The browser address bar uses https:// and displays a valid TLS security certificate for that domain
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): An HTTPS URL with a valid TLS/SSL security certificate in the browser address bar indicates that traffic between your browser and the website is encrypted in transit (p. 7).

options: A. Change default passwords immediately, keep device firmware updated, and isolate IoT devices on a separate network segment
B. Leave the factory password unchanged so the manufacturer can log in and repair the device remotely
C. Forward all router ports directly to the smart camera so you can view it without a password
D. Connect smart devices to your neighbor's open Wi-Fi network so your own router stays hidden
choices: A. Change default passwords immediately, keep device firmware updated, and isolate IoT devices on a separate network segment
B. Leave the factory password unchanged so the manufacturer can log in and repair the device remotely
C. Forward all router ports directly to the smart camera so you can view it without a password
D. Connect smart devices to your neighbor's open Wi-Fi network so your own router stays hidden
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Change default passwords immediately, keep device firmware updated, and isolate IoT devices on a separate network segment
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Changing factory-default passwords, installing firmware updates, disabling unneeded remote access, and placing IoT devices on a separate guest Wi-Fi network protect your home network (p. 6).

pamphlet_excerpts: Roadway Hazards: Surface potholes and slick sewer grates cause loss of steering control.
Hydration Planning: Riders must consume water and electrolyte fluids before feeling extreme thirst.
Concussion Assessment: Suspected head injury victims must stop riding and seek medical evaluation.
Wound Management: Clean road abrasions thoroughly with potable water before applying sterile gauze.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Route Hazard Assessment: Identify surface obstacles and narrow road shoulders prior to group departures.
Step 2 - Medical Kit Packing: Pack sterile dressings, adhesive bandages, and electrolyte powders in saddlebags.
Step 3 - Heat Stress Response: Move overheated cyclists into shade and loosen tight helmets or jerseys.
Step 4 - Incident Documentation Reporting: Record trail accident details and notify adult leadership of all injuries.

(b) Show that you know first aid for injuries or illnesses that could occur while cycling, including cuts, scratches, concussions, blisters, sunburn, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, hypothermia, frostbite, dehydration, insect stings, tick bites, and snakebite. Explain to your counselor why you should be able to identify the poisonous plants and poisonous animals that are found in your area.

pamphlet_excerpts: Vehicle Status: Bicycles hold statutory vehicle rights and must obey all traffic signals.
Lane Positioning: Ride on the right side except when turning left or passing.
Signal Communication: Extend your left arm straight horizontally to indicate an impending left turn.
Door Zone Hazards: Maintain four feet of clearance from parked cars to avoid opening doors.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Traffic Law Review: Check municipal codes regarding sidewalk bans and mandatory bicycle lane rules.
Step 2 - Shoulder Check Scan: Look over your left shoulder to confirm motor vehicle clearance before moving.
Step 3 - Hand Signal Execution: Display the hand signal clearly for three seconds prior to initiating turns.
Step 4 - Intersection Lane Control: Take the center of the travel lane when lanes are too narrow.

pamphlet_excerpts: Helmet Certification: Bicycle helmets must display a CPSC safety standard approval sticker inside.
Level Fitment: Position the front helmet rim two finger widths above the brow.
High Visibility Clothing: Fluorescent neon jerseys increase rider contrast against complex urban background environments.
Eye Protection: Clear or tinted shatterproof lenses shield eyes from grit and insects.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Helmet Placement Level: Position the helmet flat on your head without tilting backward or forward.
Step 2 - Side Strap Adjustment: Form a snug V shape directly beneath each earlobe with side sliders.
Step 3 - Chin Buckle Tension: Fasten the chinstrap allowing only one finger between strap and throat.
Step 4 - Gear Securing Protocol: Tuck loose shoelaces into shoes and secure wide pant cuffs with bands.

B. By 25 percent, which is why helmets are optional on paved bike paths
C. By 50 percent, provided the rider wears a baseball cap underneath the helmet shell
D. By 85 percent when properly sized, level on the head, and securely buckled
choices: A. By about 15 percent, and only during high-speed downhill racing crashes
B. By 25 percent, which is why helmets are optional on paved bike paths
C. By 50 percent, provided the rider wears a baseball cap underneath the helmet shell
D. By 85 percent when properly sized, level on the head, and securely buckled
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. By 85 percent when properly sized, level on the head, and securely buckled
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) data in the Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines, bicycle helmets reduce head injuries by 85 percent (p. 94).

pamphlet_excerpts: Tire Pressure: Check sidewall markings to inflate tires to their recommended pressure range.
Brake Pad Clearance: Ensure brake pads strike the wheel rim without touching the tire rubber.
Chain Lubrication: Apply bicycle lubricant to chain rollers and wipe away excess surface oil.
Quick Release Security: Close quick release levers so they curve inward and leave palm impressions.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Tire Air Inspection: Inflate inner tubes using a floor gauge pump to specified sidewall PSI.
Step 2 - Brake Squeeze Check: Squeeze brake levers to verify one thumb width clearance before bar contact.
Step 3 - Drivetrain Cleaning Lube: Degrease chain links thoroughly before applying specialized synthetic bicycle lubricant drops.
Step 4 - Cockpit Bolt Tightening: Tighten stem and seatpost binder bolts evenly to prevent unexpected slippage.

left_points: (4a) Pre-Ride Safety Inspection Points: A systematic pre-ride inspection examines wheel true, headset tightness, quick-release clamps, and cable tension. Catching loose hardware before riding prevents catastrophic mechanical failure at road speed.

(4b) Saddle and Handlebar Fitting: Set saddle height so the cyclist maintains a slight five to fifteen degree knee bend at bottom stroke. Handlebars should allow comfortable elbow flex without causing excessive spinal curvature or wrist pressure.

(4c) Brake and Derailleur Adjustment: Adjust brake barrel adjusters to remove cable slack and center the pads squarely on the rim braking track. Set derailleur high and low limit screws so the chain cannot overshoot into the spokes or frame.
right_points: (4d) Bicycle Drivetrain Lubrication Points: Apply targeted bicycle lubricant to chain pivot pins, derailleur pulleys, and brake pivot points while avoiding wheel rims. Wiping off exterior fluid keeps road grime from forming grinding paste inside moving parts.

(4e) Tire Tube Flat Repair: Repairing a flat tire involves unseating the bead with tire levers, patching or replacing the inner tube, and inspecting the tire casing. Checking the inside casing removes sharp thorns or wire fragments before reinstallation.

(4f) Bicycle Legal Compliance Standards: Local ordinances require bicycles ridden after sunset to feature a white front headlight and red rear reflector or lamp. Many jurisdictions also mandate audible warning devices like bells and functional braking systems.

rows.right: (4d) Drive train and Pivot Point Lubrication: The Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines are designed to make bicycle riding safer and more enjoyable for you and others (p. 54).

quiz_item.question: When repairing a flat tire on a ride, what critical step prevents the new or patched tube from immediately puncturing again once inflated?
options: A. Use a sharp metal screwdriver to pry the new tube over the rim bead as fast as possible
B. Carefully check the inside of the tire casing and remove the sharp object that caused the puncture, then slightly inflate the tube so it does not pinch
C. Pump the bare inner tube to 100 PSI outside the tire before forcing the tire bead onto the wheel rim
D. Coat the brake pads and wheel rims with chain lubricant so the tire slides into the frame easily

pamphlet_excerpts: Power Pedal Start: Position your dominant pedal at the two o'clock position to begin forward motion.
Threshold Emergency Braking: Shift rider body weight backward over the rear wheel during hard braking stops.
Straight Line Scanning: Practice looking over your left shoulder while keeping handlebars tracking perfectly straight.
Predictable Turning Arc: Lean bicycle gently into turns while keeping inside pedal raised at twelve.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - High Pedal Launch: Set the lead pedal to two o'clock and push down smoothly.
Step 2 - Straight Tracking Balance: Maintain steady cadence while keeping the front wheel centered within the lane.
Step 3 - Shoulder Scanning Drill: Glance backward over your shoulder without pulling the handlebar in that direction.
Step 4 - Controlled Emergency Stop: Slide weight behind saddle while squeezing both brake levers with controlled modulation.

quiz_item.question: What is the proper technique for executing an emergency stop on a bicycle without pitching over the handlebars?
options: A. Slam only the front brake lever while leaning your chest forward over the handlebars
B. Drag both feet on the pavement while letting go of the handlebars to balance
C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
D. Lock only the rear wheel into a long sideways skid while looking straight down at the front tire
choices: A. Slam only the front brake lever while leaning your chest forward over the handlebars
B. Drag both feet on the pavement while letting go of the handlebars to balance
C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
D. Lock only the rear wheel into a long sideways skid while looking straight down at the front tire
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): During an emergency stop, applying both brakes firmly while shifting your hips and body weight low and back over the rear wheel maximizes stopping power and prevents pitching over the handlebars (p. 53).

requirements.lead_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website)
requirements.req_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website) (a) Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride. (b) Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride.
sub_requirements.pamphlet_summary: The road biking option focuses on highway navigation, road safety tests, and multiple progressive endurance tours culminating in a fifty-mile ride. Cyclists must navigate traffic safely and sustain pedaling rhythm over asphalt terrain.
pamphlet_excerpts: The road biking option focuses on highway navigation, road safety tests, and multiple progressive endurance tours culminating in a fifty-mile ride. Cyclists must navigate traffic safely and sustain pedaling rhythm over asphalt terrain.

sub_requirements.workbook_visual_caption: Road Biking / Trail or Mixed Surface Biking procedures and verification checkpoints for Cycling Requirement 6.

sub_requirements.label: (b)
sub_requirements.text: Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

pamphlet_excerpts: Buddy System Discipline: Ride within conversational distance and monitor your partner for fatigue or mechanicals.
Touring Pace Cadence: Spin steady pedal cadence between seventy and ninety revolutions each minute continuously.
Trail Etiquette Rules: Yield the trail to hikers and announce passes to avoid startling horses.
Rest Stop Nutrition: Consume carbohydrate snacks and fluids every forty-five minutes during long distance rides.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Route Elevation Mapping: Chart the course profile, resupply points, and emergency bailout locations in advance.
Step 2 - Pre-Ride Buddy Briefing: Review hand signals, planned pace, and rest stop locations with your partner.
Step 3 - Cadence Nutrition Management: Maintain steady pedaling and take regular fluid sips during each ride segment.
Step 4 - Post-Ride Log Entry: Record total mileage, elapsed time, weather conditions, and terrain in your cycling logbook.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Which technique gives you the best control when riding through a tight 90-degree turn on a trail?
quiz_item.question: Which technique gives you the best control when riding through a tight 90-degree turn on a trail?
options: A. Sit back heavily on the saddle, drop the inside pedal to the ground, and lock the rear brake through the apex
B. Rise slightly off the saddle with level pedals, use bike/body separation to lean the bike, keep one finger on each brake lever, and look at your exit point
C. Take both hands off the brake levers, stare directly down at the front wheel hub, and pedal hard through the tightest part of the corner
D. Shift your shoulders far behind the rear tire while turning the handlebars sharply without leaning the bicycle frame
choices: A. Sit back heavily on the saddle, drop the inside pedal to the ground, and lock the rear brake through the apex
B. Rise slightly off the saddle with level pedals, use bike/body separation to lean the bike, keep one finger on each brake lever, and look at your exit point
C. Take both hands off the brake levers, stare directly down at the front wheel hub, and pedal hard through the tightest part of the corner
D. Shift your shoulders far behind the rear tire while turning the handlebars sharply without leaning the bicycle frame
quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Rise slightly off the saddle with level pedals, use bike/body separation to lean the bike, keep one finger on each brake lever, and look at your exit point
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Off the saddle with level pedals, pushing the bike into the turn using side-to-side bike/body separation while keeping your head up and looking at the exit point gives you balance and clearance through tight trail turns (p. 80).

requirements.description: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website) (a) Option A, Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride. (b) Option B, Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before departing on a 25-mile troop road ride, you check a Scout's helmet and notice the front rim sits high on the forehead (4 fingers above the eyebrows) and the side straps form a loose loop below the chin. How must the helmet be adjusted?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before departing on a 25-mile troop road ride, you check a Scout's helmet and notice the front rim sits high on the forehead (4 fingers above the eyebrows) and the side straps form a loose loop below the chin. How must the helmet be adjusted?
options: A. Tilt the helmet back further so the Scout can see traffic lights more easily.

B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
C. Wear a thick winter beanie underneath the loose straps without tightening the retention dial.
D. Unbuckle the chin strap during uphill climbs and refasten it only on downhill segments.
choices: A. Tilt the helmet back further so the Scout can see traffic lights more easily.

B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
C. Wear a thick winter beanie underneath the loose straps without tightening the retention dial.
D. Unbuckle the chin strap during uphill climbs and refasten it only on downhill segments.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A helmet tilted back exposes the frontal skull in a forward crash; the BSA Cycling Pamphlet's 2-V-1 fit check keeps the helmet level and secure during impact.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to safe roadway positioning guidelines, what should you do when you are riding down a street at the same speed as surrounding motor vehicle traffic?
options: A. Pull into line with the vehicles while matching their speed, and return to the right side when slower traffic resumes
B. Hop onto the pedestrian sidewalk at full speed to pass cars on the right at intersections
C. Cross the double yellow center line to ride against oncoming traffic in the left lane
D. Ride within six inches of the rear bumper of the car ahead to draft in its slip stream
choices: A. Pull into line with the vehicles while matching their speed, and return to the right side when slower traffic resumes

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Pull into line with the vehicles while matching their speed, and return to the right side when slower traffic resumes
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): When riding at the same speed as other traffic or preparing to pass or turn, cyclists pull into line with vehicles and return to the right lane once safe and convenient (p. 57).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to the NHTSA statistics in the Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines, by how much can wearing a bicycle helmet reduce the risk of head injuries?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the NHTSA statistics in the Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines, by how much can wearing a bicycle helmet reduce the risk of head injuries?
options: A. By about 15 percent, and only during high-speed downhill racing crashes
B. By 25 percent, which is why helmets are optional on paved bike paths
C. By 50 percent, provided the rider wears a baseball cap underneath the helmet shell
D. By 85 percent when properly sized, level on the head, and securely buckled
choices: A. By about 15 percent, and only during high-speed downhill racing crashes
B. By 25 percent, which is why helmets are optional on paved bike paths
C. By 50 percent, provided the rider wears a baseball cap underneath the helmet shell
D. By 85 percent when properly sized, level on the head, and securely buckled
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. By 85 percent when properly sized, level on the head, and securely buckled
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) data in the Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines, bicycle helmets reduce head injuries by 85 percent (p. 94).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When repairing a flat tire on a ride, what critical step prevents the new or patched tube from immediately puncturing again once inflated?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When repairing a flat tire on a ride, what critical step prevents the new or patched tube from immediately puncturing again once inflated?
options: A. Use a sharp metal screwdriver to pry the new tube over the rim bead as fast as possible
B. Carefully check the inside of the tire casing and remove the sharp object that caused the puncture, then slightly inflate the tube so it does not pinch
C. Pump the bare inner tube to 100 PSI outside the tire before forcing the tire bead onto the wheel rim
D. Coat the brake pads and wheel rims with chain lubricant so the tire slides into the frame easily
choices: A. Use a sharp metal screwdriver to pry the new tube over the rim bead as fast as possible
B. Carefully check the inside of the tire casing and remove the sharp object that caused the puncture, then slightly inflate the tube so it does not pinch
C. Pump the bare inner tube to 100 PSI outside the tire before forcing the tire bead onto the wheel rim
D. Coat the brake pads and wheel rims with chain lubricant so the tire slides into the frame easily
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Carefully check the inside of the tire casing and remove the sharp object that caused the puncture, then slightly inflate the tube so it does not pinch
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Before installing a patched or replacement inner tube, you must carefully inspect the inside and outside of the tire casing to remove any thorn, glass, or wire that caused the flat (p. 54).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What is the proper technique for executing an emergency stop on a bicycle without pitching over the handlebars?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What is the proper technique for executing an emergency stop on a bicycle without pitching over the handlebars?
options: A. Slam only the front brake lever while leaning your chest forward over the handlebars
B. Drag both feet on the pavement while letting go of the handlebars to balance
C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
D. Lock only the rear wheel into a long sideways skid while looking straight down at the front tire
choices: A. Slam only the front brake lever while leaning your chest forward over the handlebars
B. Drag both feet on the pavement while letting go of the handlebars to balance
C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
D. Lock only the rear wheel into a long sideways skid while looking straight down at the front tire
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Apply both brakes firmly and progressively while shifting your body weight low and back behind the saddle
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): During an emergency stop, applying both brakes firmly while shifting your hips and body weight low and back over the rear wheel maximizes stopping power and prevents pitching over the handlebars (p. 53).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which technique gives you the best control when riding through a tight 90-degree turn on a trail?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which technique gives you the best control when riding through a tight 90-degree turn on a trail?
options: A. Sit back heavily on the saddle, drop the inside pedal to the ground, and lock the rear brake through the apex
B. Rise slightly off the saddle with level pedals, use bike/body separation to lean the bike, keep one finger on each brake lever, and look at your exit point
C. Take both hands off the brake levers, stare directly down at the front wheel hub, and pedal hard through the tightest part of the corner
D. Shift your shoulders far behind the rear tire while turning the handlebars sharply without leaning the bicycle frame
choices: A. Sit back heavily on the saddle, drop the inside pedal to the ground, and lock the rear brake through the apex
B. Rise slightly off the saddle with level pedals, use bike/body separation to lean the bike, keep one finger on each brake lever, and look at your exit point
C. Take both hands off the brake levers, stare directly down at the front wheel hub, and pedal hard through the tightest part of the corner
D. Shift your shoulders far behind the rear tire while turning the handlebars sharply without leaning the bicycle frame
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Rise slightly off the saddle with level pedals, use bike/body separation to lean the bike, keep one finger on each brake lever, and look at your exit point
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Off the saddle with level pedals, pushing the bike into the turn using side-to-side bike/body separation while keeping your head up and looking at the exit point gives you balance and clearance through tight trail turns (p. 80).

intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-11-01). Dancing is a fun and exciting way to express yourself, stay active, and connect with others. Every style of dance, from hip hop and ballet to cultural and partner dances, has its own rhythm, history, and story to tell. In the Dance Test Lab Badge, you’ll learn how to move safely, warm up properly, and understand what makes every dance unique. You’ll explore different styles of dance, learn about famous dancers, and even perform your own routine. Whether you’re new to dancing or already love it, this badge will help you build confidence, creativity, and coordination while having a great time moving to the beat.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

requirements.lead_text: Preventing Injury. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Preventing Injury. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor how you can prevent injuries while participating in dancing activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. Explain what you need to take into consideration before trying potentially dangerous moves including but not limited to jumps, flips, and lifts. (b) Explain to your counselor how to appropriately warm-up prior to dancing activities to protect joints and prevent injury. Demonstrate three dance warm-ups. (c) Show that you know first aid for injuries that could occur while dancing, including cuts, scratches, abrasions, concussions, blisters, sprains, stress fractures, tendonitis, and back injuries. (d) Explain the importance of wearing the right clothing and gear for dance, including appropriate footwear.

pamphlet_excerpts: Dynamic Preparation: Active mobility exercises raise core body temperature and improve joint muscle elasticity.
Flooring Standards: Suspended wooden sprung floors absorb impact energy and shield lower leg bones.
Hydration Balance: Dancers must drink water before rehearsals to avoid sudden muscle heat cramps.
Environmental Hazards: Dancers remove floor debris and secure loose cables to prevent foot slips.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Hazard Sweep: Clear studio floor areas of loose moisture, grit, and electrical cords.
Step 2 - Thermal Warmup: Execute multi joint dynamic movements to raise core internal muscular heat.
Step 3 - Alignment Check: Position pelvis and spine neutrally to avoid excessive joint loading torque.
Step 4 - Cool Down: Perform gentle static elongation stretches after concluding all strenuous dance routines.

quiz_item.question: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
options: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.

pamphlet_excerpts: Somatic Body: Dancers articulate specific muscle groups and skeletal structures with deliberate somatic control.
Spatial Awareness: Moving along varied pathways, orientations, and levels creates complex visual choreography patterns.
Temporal Meter: Choreography modulates rhythmic tempo, syncopation, and stillness across musical beat patterns.
Dynamic Energy: Varying physical weight, flow, and muscular tension establishes expressive choreographic contrast.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Body Isolation: Articulate individual limbs while holding the central torso stable and engaged.
Step 2 - Action Pathway: Travel across the studio floor using clear directional lines and elevations.
Step 3 - Tempo Modulation: Transition smoothly between fast syncopated footwork and slow sustained physical balances.
Step 4 - Energy Alteration: Switch muscular tension from sharp explosive attacks to fluid release movements.

pamphlet_excerpts: Acrobatic Fusion: Acro dance merges classical technical dance lines with fluid gymnastic contortion skills.
Aerial Rigging: Aerialists execute vertical suspensions requiring verified weight bearing apparatus and spotters.
Classical Alignment: Ballet emphasizes turnout, erect posture, and precise foot placement positions.
Percussive Footwork: Tap dancers use metal toe and heel plates to craft complex rhythms.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Style Identification: Categorize the selected dance as solo, partner, or ensemble execution form.
Step 2 - Posture Establishment: Align the spine and feet according to the chosen genre discipline.
Step 3 - Step Demonstration: Perform representative footwork patterns and upper body stylings for the counselor.
Step 4 - Contrast Analysis: Compare technical energy qualities between two fundamentally distinct global dance traditions.

left_points: (3a) Acrobatic Dance Technique Fundamentals: Acrobatic dance combines classical dance technique with acrobatic elements and balance tricks. Performers master strength, flexibility, and transitional choreography across solo or group routines.

(3b) Aerial Apparatus Performance Methods: Aerial dance utilizes suspended apparatus like fabrics, ropes, and hoops to execute three-dimensional choreography. Dancers develop superior core strength, grip endurance, and spatial orientation above ground.

(3c) Classical Ballet Technique Traditions: Ballet features formalized terminology, external hip rotation, and precise geometrical lines. Dancers perform rigorous barre exercises, center adagios, and allegro jumps alone or partnered.
right_points: (3h) Country Western Dance Systems: Country-Western dancing encompasses two-step, waltz, and line dances performed to roots and country music. Couples travel around the perimeter of the room adhering to strict line-of-dance progression rules.

(3i) Folk Traditional Cultural Heritage: Folk and traditional dances celebrate cultural heritage, communal rites, and geographic lineage through shared choreographies. Participants often dance in circles, chains, or lines without requiring specialized theatrical backgrounds.

(3j) Hip Hop Street Dance: Hip hop dance encompasses diverse urban street styles developed alongside hip hop music and community culture. Dancers ground their weight, isolate muscle complexes, and emphasize bounce, groove, and syncopation.

requirements.lead_text: Research. Research TWO of the types of dance you learned about in requirement 3 by doing the following for EACH type of dance you chose:
requirements.req_text: Research. Research TWO of the types of dance you learned about in requirement 3 by doing the following for EACH type of dance you chose: (a) Give a brief history, including its origin, how it came to be in the United States if it originated elsewhere, and where in the world/country it is most often performed. (b) Name/describe different variations of this style of dancing, if any. (c) Name some specific types of dance steps/moves particular to this type of dance. Does this dance tell a story through movement? If so, please describe. (d) Include information on at least one person who became well-known performing, teaching, or choreographing this type of dance. (e) Note if anyone with a physical disability (such a person with hearing or sight impairment or a person who uses a wheelchair) could participate in this type of dancing. What accommodations would that person need to participate? (f) Locate and share a place near you/in your state where you could watch or participate in this type of dance as a part of a performance, competition, or class. Find out when and where this is offered and what the cost would be to watch or participate. (g) Watch a performance of this type of dance and discuss with your counselor. (While viewing an in-person performance is preferable, a recorded performance may also be permitted.)

pamphlet_excerpts: Historical Lineage: Tracing dance migration reveals how cultural traditions evolved across new global communities.
Stylistic Adaptations: Specific genres feature diverse stylistic branches adapted to theatrical or social settings.
Iconic Influences: Seminal choreographers codify foundational dance techniques that educate subsequent generations of performers.
Inclusive Movement: Adaptive dance accommodations empower individuals with physical limitations to execute artistic choreography.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - History Investigation: Document the origin location, migration pathway, and primary performing communities.
Step 2 - Movement Cataloging: Identify core technical steps, rhythmic signatures, and dramatic narrative elements.
Step 3 - Accommodation Planning: Formulate practical modifications allowing dancers with physical disabilities to participate fully.
Step 4 - Live Observation: Attend an authentic dance performance and review artistic interpretations with the counselor.

left_points: (4a) Dance Origins Cultural Migration: Researching origins uncovers how historic communities developed movement forms and transported them globally. Scouts identify international birthplaces and cultural pathways that introduced these styles to American culture.

(4b) Stylistic Variations Within Genres: Dance genres evolve into diverse substyles shaped by regional communities, competitive formats, and creative fusions. Documenting stylistic variations provides a nuanced understanding of a genre broad artistic spectrum.

(4c) Dance Vocabulary Narrative Movement: Distinct steps, hand gestures, and body shapes distinguish one dance genre from another. Scouts analyze whether these specific movement patterns communicate narrative storylines or express pure musicality.
right_points: (4d) Pioneering Choreographers Master Performers: Pioneering artists codify dance vocabularies, establish renowned training academies, and choreograph transformative performance works. Studying iconic figures illuminates the dedication, artistry, and vision required to advance the craft.

(4e) Adaptive Dance Universal Inclusion: Adaptive dance programs modify choreographic pathways, tempo cues, and partner connections for diverse abilities. Dancers utilizing wheelchairs or sensory accommodations engage fully in artistic movement and performance expression.

(4f) Local Dance Community Resources: Locating nearby dance studios, community centers, and performing arts theaters connects Scouts to regional practitioners. Exploring local venues identifies practical opportunities to engage in ongoing instruction, competitions, and viewings.

requirements.lead_text: Learn and Perform a Dance. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Learn and Perform a Dance. Do the following: (a) Learn a dance. Use at least THREE types of warm-ups prior to your routine to prepare different muscle groups for the exercise. The dance may be solo, group, or partner dance and can use a memorized choreographed routine or an improvised dance. It should be a minimum of 2 minutes long or several shorter dances that add up to at least 2 minutes. The dance should demonstrate at least three different dance moves/steps and should contain music with Scout-appropriate lyrics, if applicable. (b) Perform the dance for your counselor or submit a video of your performance to your counselor. Describe to your counselor what precautions you took to avoid injury before and during your performance. Name or describe the 3 different dance moves that you learned, the 3 different warm-ups you chose, and the 5 Elements of Dance in your routine.

pamphlet_excerpts: Phased Rehearsals: Breaking choreography into small musical counts ensures accurate technical memory retention.
Cardiovascular Pacing: Conditioning routines build necessary stamina to sustain intense energy throughout performances.
Staging Verification: Checking stage boundaries and rehearsal spacing prevents accidental collisions during routine movement.
Postural Focus: Maintaining core engagement during execution protects spinal joints during sharp directional transitions.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Warmup Execution: Complete three distinct warmup exercises targeting the core, legs, and spine.
Step 2 - Phrase Memorization: Rehearse choreographic phrases slowly with counts before dancing at full musical tempo.
Step 3 - Space Clearance: Verify safe floor clearance and boundary margins before launching into the routine.
Step 4 - Counselor Presentation: Perform the rehearsed dance routine dynamically while maintaining correct technical posture.

requirements.req_text: Careers. Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to Dance. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include , with your parent or guardian's permission , an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Educational Rigor: Dance degrees require extensive study in anatomy, kinesiology, dance history, and composition.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before starting an energetic 45-minute rehearsal involving jumps, turns, and partner lifts on a studio floor, a dancer notices a wet water spill near the center of the floor and skips warm-ups to save time. What two safety steps must happen before dancing begins?
options: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
choices: A. Dance around the wet spot at full speed and stretch only after rehearsal ends.
B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
C. Practice high-impact jumps immediately on cold muscles to warm up faster.
D. Sprinkle talcum powder over the wet puddle and attempt overhead partner lifts without a spotter.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Dry and inspect the studio floor for slip and trip hazards first, wear proper footwear, and complete a progressive cardiovascular warm-up and dynamic mobility routine.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Dynamic warm-ups increase muscle elasticity and joint synovial fluid, while a clean, dry sprung floor prevents ankle sprains and falls.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Energy
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Energy governs how movement happens, distinguishing between percussive, sustained, swinging, suspended, or collapsing movement qualities (p. 10).

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Square dancing
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Square dancing is a group social dance for four couples arranged in a square who execute steps announced live by a caller (p. 18).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How do dancers with hearing impairments often stay synchronized with musical timing during a performance?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How do dancers with hearing impairments often stay synchronized with musical timing during a performance?
options: A. By performing only in total silence without any rhythmic structure
B. By avoiding group choreography and dancing exclusively alone
C. By keeping their eyes closed throughout the entire routine
D. By feeling bass vibrations through wooden studio floors and using visual counts
choices: A. By performing only in total silence without any rhythmic structure
B. By avoiding group choreography and dancing exclusively alone
C. By keeping their eyes closed throughout the entire routine
D. By feeling bass vibrations through wooden studio floors and using visual counts
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. By feeling bass vibrations through wooden studio floors and using visual counts
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Dancers with hearing impairments commonly sense low-frequency sound vibrations through sprung wooden floors and coordinate with ensemble visual cues and internal counts (p. 24).

D. Tape both ankles tightly so the joints cannot bend
choices: A. Drink an energy beverage five minutes before stepping onto the floor

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Preparing different muscle groups with at least three distinct warmup exercises increases elasticity and coordination prior to executing your routine (p. 28).

pamphlet_excerpts: Enamel Density: Mineralized enamel blocks radiation effectively to create bright radiopaque outlines on processed film.
Carious Demineralization: Bacterial acids dissolve calcified tooth structure to show dark radiolucent shadows on radiographs.
Pulp Canal Geometry: Apical foramina permit blood vessels and nerve fibers into root canal chambers.
Alveolar Bone Crest: Healthy crestal bone margins reside two millimeters below the cementoenamel junction line.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Mount Radiograph: Position film on illuminated viewbox with identification dot facing toward observer.
Step 2 - Trace Outer Margin: Outline enamel crown and dual roots atop clean white drafting paper.
Step 3 - Detail Interior Chambers: Sketch internal pulp cavity, root canals, and surrounding periodontal ligament space.
Step 4 - Chart Decay Sites: Mark interproximal contact zones and occlusal pits where sticky plaque accumulates.

left_points: (1a) Tooth Structure and Decay: Enamel, dentin, and pulp form distinct layers with varying radiopacity under diagnostic X-ray exposure. Demineralized areas show lower density because bacterial acids have leached calcium phosphate minerals away.

(1b) Lower Molar Anatomical Diagram: Lower molars possess bifurcated mesial and distal roots anchored firmly within alveolar bone sockets by periodontal ligament fibers. Accurate technical drawings depict occlusal grooves, buccal contours, and adjacent gingival margins.
right_points: (1c) Neurovascular Pulp Entry Pathways: Sensory nerve branches and arterioles enter the root apex through minute openings called apical foramina. These vessels traverse the narrow root canal to nourish the coronal pulp chamber.

(1d) Bacterial Plaque Accumulation Sites: Biofilms adhere strongly along the gingival margin, interproximal contact areas, and deep occlusal fissures. These stagnation zones shelter bacteria from salivary rinsing and mechanical tongue action.

rows.left: (1a) Studying Tooth Structure and Decay: When one of these is damaged or missing, the tooth will loosen and eventually fall (p. 14).
rows.right: (1c) Mapping Dental Nerves and Vessels: Support for the Tooth The supportive tissues of the tooth are called theperiodontium, which includes the periodontal ligament, the alveolar bone (p. 14).

rows.left: (1b) Drawing and Labeling Molar Anatomy: The supportive tissues actually get stronger from vigorous use (p. 14).
rows.right: (1d) Locating Bacterial Plaque Accumulation Zones: The cementum, periodontal ligament, andalveolar bone connect the teeth to the jaws (p. 14).

rows.left: Effects of Tissue Damage: When one of these is damaged or missing, the tooth will loosen and eventually fall (p. 14).
rows.right: Step 3 - Label Periodontal Support Tissues: This strong, fiber like tissue anchors the root to the bone and cushions the surrounding bone against the shock of chewing and biting (p. 14).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
quiz_item.question: In Dentistry Requirement 1, how do the four main tissues of a human tooth (enamel, dentin, pulp, and cementum) function, and how does dental plaque cause a cavity (caries)?
options: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
choices: A. Pulp forms the hard outer biting shell while enamel is the soft nerve center; cavities occur when cold water cracks the cementum on the crown.
B. Dentin covers the outside of the root while enamel lines the jawbone; cavities are caused by brushing with fluoridated toothpaste.
C. Cementum is the translucent biting edge of incisors while enamel contains blood vessels; plaque protects the tooth from dietary sugars.

D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. Enamel is the hard mineralized outer crown layer, dentin is the underlying porous layer, pulp houses nerves and blood vessels, and cementum anchors the root to the periodontal ligament; bacteria in plaque biofilm ferment sugars into acids that demineralize enamel.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Enamel protects the crown over dentin and the central neurovascular pulp while cementum covers the root; cariogenic bacteria in plaque metabolize dietary carbohydrates into acids that dissolve tooth enamel unless removed by brushing, flossing, and fluoride protection.

Mouthguard Energy Absorption: Custom laminated mouthguards disperse impact force across dental arches to prevent fractures.
Avulsion Cell Preservation: Periodontal ligament cells on avulsed roots remain viable in milk for hours.
Tobacco Tissue Damage: Nicotine constricts gingival capillaries, masking early periodontal inflammation and slowing wound healing.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Retrieve Avulsed Crown: Handle knocked tooth strictly by coronal enamel without touching sensitive root cementum.
Step 2 - Rinse Debris Gently: Flush surface contaminants with saline solution without scrubbing delicate attached ligament tissues.
Step 3 - Store In Medium: Submerge tooth immediately in cold whole milk or balanced Hanks cell solution.
Step 4 - Transport To Clinic: Deliver patient and preserved tooth to dental emergency clinic within thirty minutes.
